items.passage:
Dear Ms. Grant,

My name is Jiho Lee, and I am a second-year student at Greenhill High School. I am writing on behalf of the twenty-three members of our school's Green Plate Club. Many of our members do not eat meat for health, religious, or environmental reasons, and several others would simply like to eat more vegetables. At present, however, almost every lunch on the cafeteria menu is built around meat, so these students often eat only rice and kimchi. We know that planning meals for nine hundred students is not easy, and we are grateful for the work your team does every day. Still, we would like to ask whether the cafeteria could offer one meat-free main dish at least two days a week. Our club would be happy to collect recipe ideas and survey students about which dishes they would enjoy.

Sincerely,
Jiho Lee
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 주 2회 이상 고기 없는 주요리를 제공해 달라고 요청하려고
급식 메뉴에 대한 설문 결과를 보고하려고
items.exp: 고기를 먹지 않는 학생들이 밥과 김치만 먹는 상황을 설명한 뒤, 일주일에 적어도 두 번 고기 없는 주요리를 제공해 줄 수 있는지(offer one meat-free main dish at least two days a week) 묻고 있어요. 그래서 ②가 알맞아요. 감사 표현과 설문 제안은 요청을 돕는 부분일 뿐이에요.

items.passage: Every afternoon for two months, Yuri had checked the mailbox the moment she got home from school. Her pen pal Lena, who lived in Germany, had always written back within three weeks, but this time no letter came. Yuri reread Lena's last letter again and again, looking for anything she might have said wrong. Maybe Lena had found new friends. Maybe she was simply tired of writing. Yuri sighed and closed the empty mailbox once more. Then, one rainy Friday, her mother handed her a thick envelope covered in colorful stamps. Inside were a long letter, a handmade bookmark, and a photo of Lena standing in front of a new house. "Sorry for the late reply! We moved to a new city, and I lost your address for a while," it began. Yuri laughed out loud and ran to her room to write back right away.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Yuri의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 두 달 동안 답장이 오지 않아 한숨을 쉬며 빈 우편함을 닫던 Yuri가, 이사 때문에 늦었다는 Lena의 편지와 선물을 받고 소리 내어 웃으며 바로 답장을 쓰러 달려가요. 그래서 실망했다가 기뻐하는 심경으로 바뀌어요.

items.passage: Many people visit an art museum as if they were completing a checklist. They hurry from room to room, glance at each painting for a few seconds, take a photo of the famous ones, and leave feeling tired rather than inspired. Studies of museum visitors have found that the average person spends less than half a minute in front of a single work. Yet great paintings are rarely understood at a glance. A painting that seems simple at first may reveal surprising details, colors, and feelings only after several minutes of quiet attention. So the next time you visit a museum, do not try to see everything. Choose a few works that catch your eye, sit down in front of them, and look slowly. Notice where your eyes go first, which colors stand out, and how the work makes you feel. You will leave having truly seen something, instead of having merely passed by everything.
items.q: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 미술관에서는 적은 수의 작품을 골라 오래 감상해야 한다.
미술 작품을 감상하기 전에 작가의 생애를 공부해야 한다.
미술관은 관람객이 사진을 찍지 못하게 막아야 한다.
유명한 작품부터 먼저 보는 순서로 관람해야 한다.
미술관은 관람객을 위한 휴식 공간을 늘려야 한다.
items.exp: 필자는 모든 작품을 보려 하지 말고 눈길을 끄는 몇 작품을 골라 앉아서 천천히 보라고 말해요. 그래야 단순해 보이던 그림의 세부와 느낌이 드러난다는 거예요. 사진 촬영 금지(③)는 글에서 주장하지 않아요.

items.passage: With a navigation app in our pockets, we no longer need to study maps or remember street names. We simply type in an address and follow the blue line, turn by turn. This is convenient, but it comes at a cost. Researchers have found that people who rely heavily on step-by-step directions form weaker mental maps of the places they travel through. Their eyes stay fixed on the screen rather than on the buildings, hills, and corners around them. As a result, if the phone battery dies, many people cannot find their way back even to a place they have visited many times. In earlier days, travelers who got lost had to look around, ask questions, and connect one landmark to another, and this effort built a rich picture of the area in their minds. Today, we may [arrive everywhere but know nowhere].
items.q: 밑줄 친 [arrive everywhere but know nowhere]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: travel to many places but forget the purpose of each trip
visit famous places without learning about their history
reach our destinations without understanding the places we pass through
get lost more often because maps are too complicated
depend on strangers rather than on our own sense of direction
items.exp: 길 안내 앱만 따라가면 목적지에는 도착하지만 주변 건물과 지형을 보지 않아 머릿속 지도가 약해진다는 내용이에요. 따라서 지나는 곳을 이해하지 못한 채 목적지에 도착한다는 뜻이에요. 역사 학습이나 여행 목적은 글에서 다루지 않아요.

items.passage: Along the Pacific coast of North America, underwater forests of tall seaweed called kelp provide homes for countless fish, crabs, and other sea creatures. The health of these forests depends greatly on a small, playful animal: the sea otter. Sea otters love to eat sea urchins, spiny creatures that feed on kelp. When otters disappeared from many coasts because of hunting in the nineteenth century, the number of sea urchins exploded. The urchins ate through the bottoms of the kelp, and whole forests turned into bare rocky areas. Later, when otters were protected and returned to some of these places, they began eating the urchins again. Within a few years, the kelp grew back, and fish returned with it. Scientists now call the sea otter a keystone species, an animal whose role is so important that an entire ecosystem can fall apart without it.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the reasons sea otters were hunted in the past
different kinds of seaweed in the Pacific Ocean
why sea urchins are dangerous to swimmers
methods for planting new kelp forests
the key role sea otters play in keeping kelp forests healthy
items.exp: 해달이 성게를 먹어 켈프 숲을 지키고, 해달이 사라지자 숲이 무너졌다가 돌아오자 다시 회복되었다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ⑤가 주제로 알맞아요. ①은 사냥이라는 배경에만 초점을 둔 오답이에요.

items.passage: Not long ago, buying used clothes or furniture was seen as something people did only when they could not afford new items. Today, that image is changing quickly. Online platforms make it easy to sell a jacket you no longer wear or to find a nearly new bicycle at half the price. For buyers, the benefit is obvious: they save money. But the advantages go beyond the wallet. Every time a product finds a second owner, there is one less item thrown into a landfill and one less new item that has to be manufactured, which saves energy, water, and raw materials. Some young shoppers even say they enjoy the hunt for unique items that no one else has. In this way, the secondhand market is turning old things into valuable resources and giving them a longer life.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why New Products Are Always Better
Used Goods: A Smart Choice for Wallets and the Planet
How Online Shopping Destroys Local Stores
The Hidden Costs of Recycling Old Clothes
items.exp: 중고 물품을 사면 돈을 아낄 뿐 아니라 쓰레기와 새 제품 생산을 줄여 자원을 절약한다는 내용이므로, 지갑과 지구 모두에 현명한 선택이라는 제목이 알맞아요. 지역 상점이나 유명 브랜드 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

items.passage: Edmund Thale was born in 1891 in Leeds, England, the son of a schoolteacher. As a child, he spent long winter evenings inventing word puzzles for his younger sisters. After studying at a university in London, he worked as a clerk at a newspaper, where he was asked in 1924 to fill an empty corner of the Sunday edition. He created a small crossword with only forty clues, and readers liked it so much that the paper soon made it a weekly feature. Thale became famous for clues that seemed simple but hid a second meaning, and he never used a word that could not be found in an ordinary dictionary. Although many readers sent him letters, he refused to give interviews and signed his puzzles only with the letter T. In 1950, he published a guide for young puzzle writers. He retired in 1958 and died in his hometown in 1972.
items.q: 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 어린 시절 여동생들을 위해 낱말 퍼즐을 만들었다.
1924년에 일요판의 빈 공간을 채워 달라는 요청을 받았다.
그의 크로스워드는 인기를 얻어 매주 실리게 되었다.
독자들의 요청으로 여러 차례 인터뷰에 응했다.
1950년에 젊은 퍼즐 작가들을 위한 안내서를 출판했다.
items.exp: 많은 독자가 편지를 보냈지만 그는 인터뷰를 거절하고 퍼즐에 T라는 글자로만 서명했다(refused to give interviews)고 했으므로 ④가 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 여동생들을 위한 퍼즐, 1924년의 요청, 매주 연재, 1950년의 안내서로 모두 글과 일치해요.

items.passage: Walls in early stone churches had to be very thick because they supported the heavy weight of the roof. Large windows would have weakened them, so the insides of these churches ①[were] often dark and gloomy. In the twelfth century, builders in France found a clever solution. They added stone supports outside the building, ②[known] as flying buttresses, which pressed against the walls and carried part of the roof's weight down to the ground. Because the walls no longer had to hold up the roof by ③[itself], they could be made thinner and much taller. Builders could then fill them with huge windows of colored glass, ④[which] turned ordinary sunlight into glowing pictures. Visitors ⑤[entering] these cathedrals found themselves surrounded by light and color, an experience that must have felt almost magical at a time when most buildings were dim inside. Many of these cathedrals still stand today, and their windows continue to amaze people from all over the world.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: 재귀대명사는 주어 the walls(복수)를 받아야 하므로 ③ itself를 themselves로 고쳐야 해요. ①은 복수 주어 the insides에 맞춘 were, ②는 supports를 꾸미는 과거분사, ④는 windows를 받는 관계대명사, ⑤는 Visitors를 꾸미는 현재분사라 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Gymnasts, rock climbers, and weightlifters often cover their hands with white chalk before they begin. The reason is simple: sweat makes skin slippery. Even a thin layer of moisture can ①[strengthen] the grip between the hands and a bar or a rock, and a hand that slides at the wrong moment can lead to a serious fall. The chalk athletes use is not the kind teachers write with but a powder called magnesium carbonate, which ②[absorbs] moisture very quickly. By keeping the palms dry, it allows the skin to hold the surface more ③[firmly]. However, more is not always better. Too much chalk can form a loose layer of dust that actually ④[reduces] contact with the surface. Experienced climbers therefore apply a small amount and brush off the extra. Some climbing areas even ask visitors to use colored chalk, because white marks left on natural rock can ⑤[spoil] the view for others.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 땀이 피부를 미끄럽게 만든다고 했으므로 얇은 수분층은 손과 봉·바위 사이의 마찰을 강화하는(strengthen) 것이 아니라 약화해야(weaken) 해요. ② absorbs와 ③ firmly는 초크가 손을 건조하게 해 단단히 잡게 한다는 내용과 맞고, ④ reduces는 지나친 초크의 부작용을 나타내요.

items.passage: In a weak picture book, the pictures simply show what the words already say. If the text reads, "The girl climbed the tree," the picture shows a girl in a tree, and the reader gains nothing new. In the best picture books, however, words and pictures work like two voices in a conversation. The text might say, "Nothing ever happens on my street," while the pictures show a giraffe walking past the window and a spaceship landing in the park. Young readers notice the gap and laugh, proud that they can see what the narrator cannot. In other books, the pictures quietly show a character's fear while the words claim she is brave. Such books invite children to compare, question, and think. For this reason, many authors and illustrators agree that a good picture should never merely ___ the words; it should add something the words leave unsaid.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 약한 그림책은 글이 이미 말한 것을 그림이 그대로 보여 줄 뿐이고, 좋은 그림책의 그림은 글이 말하지 않은 것을 더한다고 했어요. 따라서 좋은 그림은 글을 단지 되풀이(repeat)해서는 안 돼요. contradict나 enrich는 오히려 좋은 그림책이 하는 일이에요.

items.passage: Imagine a sign in a library that says, "No talking." Clearly, a group of friends chatting loudly about their weekend should stop. But what about a student who quietly asks the librarian where to find a book, a visitor who shouts "Fire!" after seeing smoke, or a blind reader using a machine that reads books aloud in a soft voice? The words of the sign alone cannot settle these cases. To decide, we have to ask why the rule exists in the first place: to allow people to read and study without being disturbed. Once we see this, the answers become clear. The quiet question disturbs almost no one, the warning protects the very people the rule is meant to serve, and the reading machine actually helps someone read. A person who applies the rule only to its exact words might scold the visitor who warned about the fire while proudly saying that he was following the rules. This shows that following a rule wisely requires ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: obeying its words exactly, whatever the situation
understanding the purpose it was created to serve
asking the people in charge before taking any action
making new rules whenever an unusual case appears
considering how many people have agreed to follow it
items.exp: 표지판의 문구만으로는 판단할 수 없고 규칙이 왜 만들어졌는지(방해받지 않고 읽고 공부하게 하려는 것)를 물어야 답이 분명해진다고 했어요. 그래서 규칙을 지혜롭게 따르려면 그 목적을 이해해야 해요. ①은 글이 비판하는 태도이고, ④처럼 새 규칙을 만들자는 말은 없어요.

items.passage: In almost every sport, teams tend to win more often when they play at home than when they play away, and researchers have suggested several reasons for this pattern. ① One obvious reason is the support of the crowd, whose cheers can lift the players' energy and confidence at important moments. ② Home players also know their own field or court very well, including how the ball bounces and how the wind usually blows. ③ In addition, visiting teams often have to travel long distances, and tiredness from the journey can affect their performance. ④ Ticket prices for popular home games have risen sharply in recent years, making it hard for many families to attend. ⑤ Some studies even suggest that referees, influenced by the noise of thousands of home fans, may make slightly more decisions in favor of the home team without realizing it.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 홈 경기에서 더 자주 이기는 이유(관중 응원, 경기장 익숙함, 원정 피로, 심판 판정)를 나열하는 글인데, ④는 홈 경기 입장권 가격이 올랐다는 내용이라 승리 이유와 관계가 없어요.

items.passage:
Before a concert begins, the members of an orchestra play a single note together, filling the hall with a long, steady sound. This short moment of tuning is not just a habit; it makes sure that every instrument agrees on exactly the same pitch.

(A) Even after all this, the work is not completely finished. As the hall warms up during a long performance, some instruments slowly go out of tune, so players often make small adjustments between pieces.

(B) The note is usually given by the oboe. Its sound is clear and bright, so it can be heard easily above the other instruments, and its pitch is also hard to change quickly, which makes it a dependable starting point.

(C) Once the oboe has sounded this note, the other players adjust their instruments to match it, usually section by section. The woodwinds and brass go first, and then the strings, which can need a little more time.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 주어진 글의 a single note를 The note로 받아 오보에가 음을 낸다고 소개하는 (B)가 먼저 와요. 그다음 오보에가 this note를 내면 나머지 악기들이 맞춘다는 (C)가 이어지고, 이 모든 과정(all this) 뒤에도 공연 중 음을 다시 맞춘다는 (A)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: When traveling abroad, many people are unsure whether they should leave a tip, and the answer depends greatly on where they are. ( ① ) In the United States, tipping is a strong social expectation in restaurants, taxis, and hotels. ( ② ) Servers in many restaurants earn a fairly low basic wage, so customers usually add 15 to 20 percent of the bill for them. ( ③ ) In Japan, by contrast, leaving extra money on the table can actually cause confusion. ( ④ ) Many Japanese people believe that excellent service is simply part of the job and is already included in the price. ( ⑤ ) In fact, a restaurant worker may even run after a customer to return money that he or she seems to have forgotten. Learning these customs before a trip can save travelers from awkward moments and help them show respect for local culture.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

Because these tips make up a large part of their income, leaving nothing is often considered rude.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 these tips와 their income은 손님이 더해 주는 15~20퍼센트의 팁과 기본급이 낮은 종업원을 가리켜요. 그래서 그 문장 바로 뒤, 일본 이야기가 시작되기 전인 ③에 들어가야 해요. ②에는 their가 가리킬 대상이 아직 없어요.

items.passage: On a winter day, the thermometer may read zero degrees, yet a strong wind can make it feel far colder. The moving air itself is no colder than still air, so why is there a difference? The answer lies in a thin layer of warm air that our bodies constantly create. Heat leaving the skin warms the air right next to it, forming an invisible blanket that slows down further heat loss. On a calm day, this layer stays in place and protects us. When the wind blows, however, it keeps sweeping the warm layer away and replacing it with cold air, so the body must keep giving up heat to warm the new air. The stronger the wind, the faster this happens. This is why weather reports often give a "feels like" temperature, and why a thin windproof jacket can keep you warmer than a thick sweater that lets air pass through.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Wind makes us feel colder not by (A) ___ the temperature of the air but by (B) ___ the warm layer of air around our skin.
items.exp: 움직이는 공기가 정지한 공기보다 더 차갑지는 않다고 했으므로 바람은 기온을 낮추는(lowering) 것이 아니에요. 바람이 피부 주변의 따뜻한 공기층을 계속 쓸어 가므로(B)는 removing이 알맞아요. thickening은 공기층을 두껍게 한다는 뜻이라 반대예요.

items.passage:
Every language borrows words from other languages. English, for example, took "piano" from Italian, "ballet" from French, and "tsunami" from Japanese. Korean has also absorbed many foreign words, such as "computer" and "bus." Some people worry that this borrowing will (a)[weaken] their language and that, one day, it may lose its unique character. However, the history of languages suggests the opposite.

When a language borrows a word, it rarely takes it over unchanged. The word is usually (b)[adapted] to fit the sounds and grammar of its new home. Japanese speakers, for instance, turned the English "ice cream" into "aisukurimu," adding vowels to suit their sound system. Over time, borrowed words become so familiar that most speakers no longer think of them as foreign at all. Few English speakers realize that everyday words like "sky" and "egg" came from the language of Viking settlers more than a thousand years ago.

Borrowing also allows a language to (c)[express] new ideas quickly. When new inventions, foods, or customs arrive from abroad, speakers need names for them, and taking an existing word is often easier than creating a completely new one. In this sense, loanwords are like windows that let in fresh air from other cultures.

Of course, using too many foreign words when good native words already exist can make communication (d)[clearer] for some listeners, especially older people. But a language that refuses all outside influence would (e)[struggle] to keep up with a changing world. A living language, like a living body, grows by taking in nourishment from outside and making it part of itself.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Foreign Words Should Be Banned
The Difficulty of Learning Japanese Sounds
Older People and the Fear of New Words
Borrowed Words: Fresh Air That Keeps Languages Alive
items.exp: 외래어 차용은 언어를 약하게 하는 것이 아니라, 새 언어에 맞게 바뀌며 새로운 생각을 표현하게 해 주는 신선한 공기 같다고 했어요. 그래서 ⑤가 알맞아요. 바이킹 이야기는 예시일 뿐이고 문법이 아니라 낱말 이야기예요.

items.exp: 필요 이상의 외래어는 일부 청자, 특히 어르신들에게 의사소통을 더 어렵게 할 수 있다는 흐름이므로 (d) clearer는 harder 같은 낱말로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 문맥에 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Leo had never taken a long train trip alone. When his parents put him on the overnight train to visit his aunt in the mountains, he held his ticket tightly and found his seat by the window. Across from him sat an elderly man with a small paper bag on his lap. The man nodded kindly, but Leo was too nervous to say anything. He put on his headphones and stared out at the city lights disappearing behind the train.

(B)
When Leo woke up, sunlight was pouring through the window and the train was pulling into his station. The seat across from him was empty; (a)[his new friend] must have gotten off at an earlier stop. On the seat lay the paper bag, and inside was a shiny silver whistle with a note: "For the bravest traveler on this line. Keep looking up at the stars." Leo smiled and put the whistle in his pocket. As he stepped onto the platform, he saw his aunt waving, and he ran toward her with a story he could not wait to tell.

(C)
About two hours into the journey, the train suddenly slowed down and came to a stop in the middle of a dark forest. The lights flickered and went out. Leo pulled off his headphones, his heart pounding. "Don't worry," said the old man in a calm voice. "It's probably just a signal problem. They'll fix it soon." Leo asked the old man how (b)[he] could be so sure. The old man laughed softly. "Because I drove trains on this very line for thirty-five years," he answered.

(D)
Leo's fear began to fade as (c)[the man] described his years as a train driver: the snowstorms (d)[he] had driven through and the deer that sometimes stood on the tracks. The old man opened his paper bag and shared his homemade sandwiches with Leo. When the train finally started moving again, he pointed at the sky. Without the city lights, thousands of stars were shining above the forest. Leo had never seen anything like it. Listening to more stories, (e)[he] gradually fell asleep with his head against the window.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: (A)에서 Leo가 노인 맞은편에 앉은 뒤, 기차가 숲에서 멈추고 노인이 기관사였다고 밝히는 (C), 그 기관사 시절 이야기를 듣고 잠드는 (D), 아침에 깨어 보니 노인이 떠나고 호루라기가 남아 있는 (B) 순서가 알맞아요.

items.passage:
Dear Volunteers,

Thank you all for signing up for the Willow Creek Park Clean-Up Day, which was scheduled for this Saturday, May 15. We were excited to see that over eighty people had registered, the largest number in the history of our event. Unfortunately, the weather service has just announced that heavy rain and strong winds are expected all weekend. Working near the creek in such conditions could be dangerous, and the wet ground would make it difficult to collect trash safely. For these reasons, we have decided to move the event to the following Saturday, May 22. The meeting time and place will remain the same: 9 a.m. at the main gate. Your registration will be carried over automatically, so you do not need to sign up again. We apologize for any inconvenience and hope to see you all next week.

Best regards,
Daniel Brooks
Willow Creek Community Center
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 공원 정화 활동의 참가 신청 방법을 안내하려고
악천후로 인한 공원 정화 행사 연기를 알리려고
items.exp: 주말에 폭우와 강풍이 예보되어 공원 정화 행사를 다음 주 토요일로 옮긴다고 알리는 글이에요. 집합 시간과 장소는 그대로라고 했으므로 장소 변경 공지는 틀려요.

items.passage: Jiyoon stood in front of the mirror at the eye clinic and frowned. The round black frames made her face look like someone else's. "Everyone at school will laugh at me," she thought, and she kept her head down as she followed her mother outside. Then she looked up. The tree across the street was not a green cloud anymore. She could see every single leaf, each one moving on its own in the wind. The letters on a shop sign far down the road were sharp and clear, and she could even read the number on a bus before it reached the stop. "Mom, look! Trees have leaves!" she shouted, and her mother laughed. Jiyoon turned around in a slow circle, staring at everything, and suddenly she did not care at all what her new glasses looked like.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Jiyoon의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 처음에는 새 안경을 쓴 모습을 보고 학교에서 놀림받을까 걱정하며 고개를 숙였어요. 밖에서 나뭇잎 하나하나와 먼 간판까지 또렷이 보이자 소리치며 모든 것을 바라보았으므로 놀라워한 거예요. 그래서 worried → amazed가 알맞아요.

items.passage: On old stone walls and tree bark, you may notice flat patches of gray, green, or orange. They look like a single plant, but a lichen is actually two very different living things growing as one. One partner is a fungus, which cannot make its own food. The other is a tiny alga, which can make sugar from sunlight but quickly dries out on bare rock. Inside a lichen, the fungus builds a tough body that holds water and shields the alga from strong sunlight and wind. In return, the alga feeds the fungus with the sugar it produces. Neither could survive alone in such harsh places, yet together they live on mountain tops, desert rocks, and even frozen Antarctic stones. A lichen, then, is [a house built by one and lit by the other]. It reminds us that in nature, survival does not always depend on competition.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [a house built by one and lit by the other]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: a living thing that gets its energy only by breaking down rocks
a partnership in which one gives shelter and the other produces food
a plant that grows only where there is plenty of light and water
a fungus that slowly takes over and destroys the alga inside it
a group of organisms that compete with one another for sunlight
items.exp: 곰팡이(균류)는 물을 머금은 튼튼한 몸을 만들어 조류를 보호하고, 조류는 햇빛으로 당을 만들어 곰팡이에게 먹이를 준다고 했어요. 그래서 '한쪽은 집을 짓고 다른 쪽은 불을 밝힌다'는 한쪽은 보금자리를, 다른 쪽은 먹이를 주는 협력 관계를 뜻해요. 필자는 생존이 늘 경쟁에 달린 것은 아니라고 했으므로 ⑤는 반대예요.

items.passage: When a task seems huge, such as writing a long report or cleaning an extremely messy room, many people keep putting it off. The problem is not always laziness. Looking at the whole job at once can make us feel overwhelmed, and our brain responds by avoiding it. One effective way to get started is to break the task into small, clear steps. Instead of telling yourself, "I have to write the report," you might decide, "I will find three sources today." Instead of "I have to clean my room," you might say, "I will put away just the books on the floor." Each small step feels easy to begin, and finishing it gives you a sense of progress. That feeling, in turn, gives you the energy to take the next step. Before long, the job that once looked impossible is nearly done.
items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 어려운 일일수록 다른 사람의 도움을 받아야 한다.
보고서를 쓸 때는 자료 조사가 가장 중요하다.
큰 일은 작은 단계로 나누면 시작하고 끝내기 쉬워진다.
방 청소는 정해진 순서에 따라 하는 것이 좋다.
items.exp: 큰 일을 한꺼번에 보면 압도되어 미루게 되지만, 작고 분명한 단계로 나누면 시작하기 쉽고 진전의 느낌이 다음 단계로 이끈다는 것이 요지예요. 미루는 것이 꼭 게으름 때문은 아니라고 했으므로 ②는 틀려요.

items.passage: A rainbow often appears when the sun comes out right after a shower, but it is not an object hanging in the sky. It is created by sunlight and millions of tiny raindrops. Sunlight looks white, but it is actually a mixture of many colors. When a ray of sunlight enters a raindrop, it bends, and each color bends by a slightly different amount. The light then bounces off the back of the drop and bends again as it comes out. As a result, the colors spread apart, with red on the outside and violet on the inside. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the rain in front of you. Because the angle between the sun, the drops, and your eyes matters, two people standing in different places actually see light from different raindrops. In a sense, everyone sees his or her own rainbow.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the reason rain often falls after sunny weather
why the sky turns red at sunset
old stories people told about rainbows
ways to take clear photos of rainbows
how sunlight and raindrops form a rainbow
items.exp: 햇빛이 빗방울 속에서 꺾이고 반사되며 색이 나뉘어 무지개가 생기고, 서 있는 위치에 따라 서로 다른 빗방울의 빛을 본다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ⑤가 주제로 알맞아요. ②의 노을은 글에 나오지 않아요.

items.passage: Your grandparents probably owned a radio or a washing machine that lasted for decades. When something broke, they opened it up with a screwdriver, replaced the broken part, and kept using it. Many of today's devices are very different. Smartphones and laptops are often sealed with glue, and their batteries cannot be removed easily. Replacement parts can be hard to find, and some companies allow only their own service centers to fix their products. As a result, when a small part fails, many people simply throw away the entire device and buy a new one. This adds to the growing mountain of electronic waste, which contains harmful materials. In response, some governments have begun to require companies to make products that ordinary people and local shops can repair more easily.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Built to Be Thrown Away? The Problem of Unrepairable Devices
How to Choose the Best Smartphone
The Fast Growth of Online Service Centers
New Batteries That Last for Decades
items.exp: 예전 물건과 달리 요즘 기기는 접착제로 봉해져 고치기 어려워 통째로 버려지고 전자 폐기물이 늘어난다는 문제를 다루므로 ①이 알맞아요. 라디오 음질이나 배터리 수명 이야기는 없어요.

items.passage:

items.q: Seabrook Tide Pool Discovery Day 2027에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 7세에서 13세 어린이가 부모와 함께 참가할 수 있다.
items.exp: 준비물에 젖어도 되는 신발을 가져오되 샌들은 안 된다(no sandals)고 했으므로 ④가 안내문과 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 시간, 대상, 참가비, 취소 조건의 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage: Long before paper was invented in China, the ancient Egyptians had already found a way to make a writing material from a plant called papyrus. This tall plant grew ①[thickly] along the banks of the Nile River. Workers cut its stems into thin strips and laid them side by side. Then they placed a second layer of strips across the first one and ②[pressed] the two layers together. The plant's natural juices acted like glue, and once the sheet ③[had dried] in the sun, it became smooth and strong. Sheets could be joined to form long rolls, some of ④[which] were more than twenty meters long. Papyrus was so useful that it was sold to many other countries around the Mediterranean Sea. Thanks to the dry climate of Egypt, some documents ⑤[writing] on papyrus thousands of years ago have survived to this day.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: ⑤는 문서가 '쓰인' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 written이 되어야 해요. ①은 동사 grew를 꾸미는 부사, ②는 placed와 병렬, ③은 과거완료, ④는 전치사 of 뒤의 관계대명사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: When you cut an apple and leave it on the table, the white flesh soon turns brown. This change does not mean that the fruit has ①[spoiled]; the brown apple is still safe to eat. Inside the apple's cells, certain proteins called enzymes are normally kept ②[together] with natural chemicals stored in other parts of the cell. When a knife breaks the cells open, these substances ③[mix] and react with oxygen in the air, producing the brown color. This browning may actually help the plant, since the brown compounds can ④[protect] a damaged fruit from insects and germs. If you want to keep apple slices looking fresh, you can dip them in lemon juice. Its acid slows the enzymes down, so the fruit stays ⑤[pale] for much longer.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 칼이 세포를 깨뜨려야 효소와 화학 물질이 섞여 갈색이 된다고 했으므로, 평소에는 둘이 세포의 다른 부분에 따로 떨어져 있어야 해요. 그래서 ② together를 separate(따로)로 바꿔야 해요. 레몬즙의 산이 효소를 느리게 해 과일이 밝은 색(pale)을 유지한다는 ⑤는 알맞아요.

items.passage: Think about the last time you walked through a well-designed door. You probably did not think about it at all. You saw a flat metal plate and pushed, or you saw a handle and pulled, and you went through without slowing down. Now think about a door that has the same handle on both sides but opens only one way. You pull, nothing happens, and you feel a little foolish as you try again. Designers point out that we tend to become aware of an object only when it fails to work the way we expect. A light switch, a ticket machine, or a website menu that is easy to use simply lets us do what we want, so our attention stays on our goal rather than on the object. In this sense, the highest praise for a designer is that people using the product never ___ the design at all.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 잘 만든 문은 생각할 필요도 없이 지나가고, 물건은 기대대로 작동하지 않을 때만 의식하게 된다고 했어요. 그래서 디자이너에게 최고의 칭찬은 사람들이 디자인을 아예 알아차리지(notice) 못하는 것이에요. depend on은 사용자가 물건을 쓰며 의지한다는 뜻이라 글과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: We often picture scientists as people who are sure about everything. In reality, the strength of science comes from the opposite attitude. A good scientist does not simply look for evidence that supports a favorite idea. Instead, she designs experiments that could show the idea is wrong, and then she checks the results honestly. If the idea survives many such tests, people can trust it more. If it fails, it is changed or thrown away, even if a famous researcher proposed it. For centuries, for example, many people believed that heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones, until careful experiments showed otherwise. This process can feel uncomfortable, because nobody likes being told that they are mistaken. Yet it is exactly what allows knowledge to improve over time. A field in which no idea could ever be questioned would stop moving forward. In this sense, science makes progress not because scientists are always right, but because they ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: rely on the opinions of famous researchers
collect only the evidence that supports their ideas
avoid experiments that might produce unexpected results
are willing to test their ideas and admit when they are wrong
explain their theories in ways that ordinary people can understand
items.exp: 과학자는 자기 생각이 틀렸음을 보여 줄 수 있는 실험을 하고, 실패하면 생각을 바꾸거나 버리며, 이 과정 덕분에 지식이 발전한다고 했어요. 그래서 생각을 검증하고 틀렸을 때 인정한다는 ④가 알맞아요. ②③은 글이 비판하는 태도이고, ①은 유명한 학자의 생각도 버려진다는 내용과 반대예요.

items.passage: Water makes up more than half of the human body, and even mild dehydration can affect how we feel and think. ① When we lose just one or two percent of our body's water, we may begin to feel tired, have headaches, or find it hard to concentrate. ② Bottled water has become one of the most popular drinks in the world, and companies sell billions of bottles every year. ③ Thirst is a useful signal, but it often appears only after the body is already slightly dehydrated. ④ This is why doctors recommend drinking water regularly throughout the day rather than waiting until we feel thirsty. ⑤ Eating fruits and vegetables with high water content, such as watermelon and cucumbers, can also help us stay well hydrated.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 가벼운 탈수도 몸과 생각에 영향을 주므로 갈증을 느끼기 전에 물을 자주 마셔야 한다는 흐름인데, ②는 생수가 세계적으로 많이 팔린다는 판매 이야기라 흐름에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
The Venus flytrap is a plant that catches insects with leaves shaped like a pair of jaws. Yet the trap does not close every time something touches it.

(A) Inside each leaf are a few tiny trigger hairs. If an insect brushes against one hair only once, nothing happens. The trap snaps shut only when the hairs are touched twice within about twenty seconds.

(B) Even after the trap has closed, the counting continues. As the trapped insect struggles, it touches the hairs again and again, and only after several more touches does the plant begin to release digestive juices. In this way, it avoids wasting its precious juices on something it cannot eat.

(C) This counting system saves the plant from closing for nothing. A falling raindrop or a blown leaf usually touches a hair just once, whereas a living insect walking around inside the leaf keeps bumping into the hairs.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 덫이 건드려질 때마다 닫히지는 않는다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 감각털이 20초 안에 두 번 닿아야 닫힌다는 (A)가 와요. 이 세기 방식(This counting system)이 빗방울 같은 것에 헛되이 닫히지 않게 해 준다는 (C)가 이어지고, 덫이 닫힌 뒤에도 세기가 계속된다(Even after the trap has closed)는 (B)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: Bike-sharing programs have spread to hundreds of cities around the world. ( ① ) Users can unlock a bicycle with a smartphone app, ride it across town, and leave it at another station near their destination. ( ② ) For short trips, this is often faster than waiting for a bus and cheaper than taking a taxi. ( ③ ) The programs also reduce traffic and air pollution, and they encourage people to get more exercise in their daily lives. ( ④ ) However, the systems face some practical challenges. ( ⑤ ) To solve this, operators use trucks to move bikes from crowded stations to empty ones, and some offer small rewards to users who return bikes to stations where they are needed. With such efforts, bike sharing can become a reliable part of city transportation.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

In the morning, for example, bikes tend to pile up at stations near offices, while stations in residential areas are left empty.
items.exp: 주어진 문장은 However 뒤에 나온 '실제적인 어려움'의 구체적인 예(자전거가 한쪽에 몰리는 문제)예요. 그 뒤의 To solve this가 이 문제를 받으므로 ⑤에 들어가야 해요.

items.passage: When a group of meerkats searches for food, they spend most of their time digging in the sand with their heads down, looking for insects and small animals. This leaves them open to attack from eagles and jackals. To deal with this danger, one member of the group usually climbs onto a rock or a small bush and stands on its back legs to keep watch. While the others eat, this guard scans the sky and the land around them. If it spots a predator, it gives a sharp call, and all the meerkats run to the nearest hole. Different calls even tell the group whether the danger is coming from the air or from the ground. After about an hour, another member takes over the job, so that the guard can also have a chance to eat.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Meerkats protect their group while feeding by having one member act as a (A) ___ and by taking (B) ___ at this role.
items.exp: 한 마리가 높은 곳에서 망을 보며(lookout) 포식자를 알리고, 약 한 시간마다 다른 개체가 그 일을 넘겨받아 번갈아(turns) 맡는다고 했어요. hunter나 leader는 망을 보는 역할과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage:
After a harvest, many farmers leave their fields bare until the next planting season. It may seem natural to let the land rest, but bare soil is actually (a)[vulnerable]. Heavy rain can wash away the top layer, which contains most of the nutrients plants need, and strong winds can blow dry soil into the air. Without plant roots to hold it together, soil that took hundreds of years to form can be lost in just a few seasons.

To prevent this, a growing number of farmers are planting what are called cover crops, such as clover, rye, or beans, during the months when no main crop is growing. These plants are not grown to be sold. Instead, their roots (b)[grip] the soil and keep it in place, and their leaves protect the ground from pounding rain.

Cover crops offer other benefits as well. Some of them, especially beans and clover, can take nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which (c)[reduces] the need for chemical fertilizers. When the cover crops are cut down and left on the field, they decay and turn into natural food for the soil. They also block sunlight from reaching weed seeds, so fewer weeds (d)[sprout] in spring.

Of course, planting cover crops takes extra time and money, and the benefits may not appear in the first year. However, farmers who have used them for many years report healthier soil and more (e)[unstable] harvests. In this way, giving the soil a green blanket today is an investment in the food we will eat tomorrow.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Cover Crops: A Green Blanket That Protects the Soil
Why Farmers Should Sell More Beans
The Dangers of Chemical Fertilizers in Cities
How Weeds Help Crops Grow Faster
Rainfall Patterns and the Planting Season
items.exp: 수확 후 맨땅으로 두면 흙이 유실되지만, 피복작물을 심으면 흙을 붙잡고 영양분을 더하며 잡초를 줄인다는 내용이므로 ①이 알맞아요. 피복작물은 팔려고 기르는 것이 아니라고 했으므로 ②는 틀려요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 피복작물을 오래 쓴 농부들이 더 건강한 흙을 얻었다는 긍정적인 흐름이므로 (e) unstable은 stable이나 abundant 같은 낱말로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 문맥에 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Sam had been on the Westfield High soccer team for two years, but he had played in only a few minutes of real games. Most of the time, he sat on the bench, filled water bottles, and watched. But Sam did not simply watch. He carried a small notebook and wrote down everything he noticed about the other teams: which players liked to dribble, which ones always passed, and how each goalkeeper moved.

(B)
The first half was difficult. Sam missed an easy pass, and the other team scored, taking a 1–0 lead. At halftime, the players sat silently in the locker room. Then Sam opened (a)[his] notebook and walked over to the coach. "Their goalkeeper always leaves his line early when someone runs at him," he said. "If I chip the ball over him, I think it will go in." Coach Harris looked at the notes, thought for a moment, and nodded.

(C)
Ten minutes into the second half, Sam got the ball near the penalty area. Just as (b)[he] had predicted, the goalkeeper rushed forward. Sam lifted the ball gently over his head, and it dropped into the net. The crowd roared. Five minutes before the end, Sam used another note to set up the winning goal for a teammate. When the final whistle blew, the players lifted (c)[him] onto their shoulders. From the bench, Marco shouted, "I told you you were ready!"

(D)
The day before the championship final, the team's star striker, Marco, twisted his ankle during practice. Coach Harris looked worried as (d)[he] studied the list of remaining players. To everyone's surprise, he chose Sam to take Marco's place. Sam's hands went cold. "Me? I'm not ready," he said. Marco, sitting with ice on his ankle, smiled at (e)[him]. "You know more about these teams than any of us. Just trust your notes."
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 벤치에서 상대 팀을 기록하던 Sam의 이야기 (A) 뒤에, 결승 전날 Marco가 다쳐 Sam이 대신 뽑히는 (D), 전반전에 뒤진 채 하프타임에 Sam이 공책 내용을 코치에게 말하는 (B), 후반전에 그 예측대로 골을 넣고 승리하는 (C) 순서가 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?

items.q: 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Sam은 2년 동안 실제 경기에 거의 출전하지 못했다.
Sam은 전반전에 쉬운 패스를 성공시켜 동점을 만들었다.
Sam은 상대 골키퍼의 키를 넘기는 슛으로 골을 넣었다.
Marco는 결승 전날 연습 중 발목을 다쳤다.
items.exp: (B)에서 Sam은 전반전에 쉬운 패스를 놓쳤고 상대 팀이 골을 넣어 1대 0으로 앞섰다고 했으므로 ②가 틀려요. 나머지는 모두 글과 일치해요.

items.passage:
Dear Mr. Harrison,

My name is Clara Benson, and I have lived in Unit 4B of Westbrook Apartments for six years. I am writing on behalf of several residents who ride bicycles to work and school. At present, there is no safe place to keep our bikes. Many of us carry them up the stairs and store them in our narrow hallways, which makes it hard for others to pass. Some residents lock their bikes to the fence near the entrance, but two bikes were badly damaged by rain and snow last winter. We have noticed that the corner of the underground parking area next to the elevator is rarely used. If a simple bike rack could be put there, it would solve the problem without taking away any parking spaces. We would be happy to share the cost if necessary. Thank you for considering our request.

Sincerely,
Clara Benson
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 필자는 자전거를 둘 안전한 곳이 없다는 문제를 설명한 뒤, 지하 주차장 구석에 간단한 자전거 보관대를 설치해 달라고 부탁하고 있어요. 비용 분담 의사까지 밝히며 요청하므로 ②가 정답이에요. 자전거가 비에 망가졌다는 내용은 있지만 도난 신고는 아니에요.

items.passage: It was my first time babysitting alone, and the Parks had been gone for only twenty minutes when their baby, Noah, started to cry. I checked his diaper. It was dry. I offered him his bottle, but he pushed it away and screamed even louder. I walked around the living room, bouncing him gently, but his face only grew redder. My arms ached, and I kept glancing at the phone, wondering whether I should call his parents and admit that I could not handle it. Then I remembered something Mrs. Park had mentioned at the door: Noah loved the sound of the washing machine. I carried him to the laundry room, started an empty load, and sat on the floor with him in my lap. Within minutes, his cries became soft hiccups, and then his eyes slowly closed. I leaned back against the wall and smiled. I had done it on my own.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 I의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 아기가 계속 울어 팔이 아프고 부모에게 전화해 못 하겠다고 말할까 고민할 만큼 어쩔 줄 몰랐던 I는, 세탁기 소리로 아기를 재운 뒤 미소 지으며 혼자 해냈다고 느껴요. 그래서 helpless → satisfied인 ④가 알맞아요. 처음부터 침착하지 않았으므로 ③은 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: In most classrooms, the teacher asks the questions and the students answer them. This pattern seems natural, but it leaves students with only half of the thinking process. Answering a question requires finding information, while asking a good question requires understanding what you do not yet know. That second skill is just as important, and it is rarely practiced. When students are asked to write their own questions about a lesson, they must look at the material from a new angle. They notice gaps in their understanding and start to wonder about connections between ideas. Their questions also show the teacher what they are confused about, which a test score cannot do. So instead of ending every lesson with a quiz, teachers should regularly give students time to make their own questions and share them with classmates. Learning to ask is, in the end, part of learning itself.
items.q: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 수업이 끝날 때마다 퀴즈로 학습 내용을 점검해야 한다.
교사는 학생의 질문에 즉시 정확한 답을 제시해야 한다.
학생들이 다른 학생의 질문에 답하는 시간을 늘려야 한다.
시험 점수보다 수업 태도를 더 중시하여 평가해야 한다.
교사는 학생들이 스스로 질문을 만들어 보게 해야 한다.
items.exp: 필자는 질문을 만드는 능력도 답하는 능력만큼 중요하다고 하며, 교사가 학생들에게 스스로 질문을 만들고 나눌 시간을 주어야 한다고 주장해요. 그래서 ⑤가 정답이에요. 필자는 매 수업을 퀴즈로 끝내는 대신 질문 만들기를 하라고 했으므로 ①은 반대 진술이에요.

items.passage: When we scroll through other people's posts, we see their best moments: the perfect vacation, the award ceremony, the beautifully served dinner. What we do not see are the hours of practice, the arguments, or the burnt dishes that never made it onto the screen. Meanwhile, we know every detail of our own messy lives. We know about the dirty pans, the failed attempts, and the days when nothing went right. Comparing ourselves to others online is therefore like [measuring your kitchen against their restaurant]. One is a place where things are prepared, tested, and sometimes thrown away; the other is a place where only the finished product is shown to guests. The comparison is unfair from the start, and it is no surprise that we usually feel we have lost. Remembering this difference will not stop us from looking, but it can help us look with more realistic eyes.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [measuring your kitchen against their restaurant]이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: trying to copy other people's lifestyles without enough money
judging others' lives only by the food they choose to eat
comparing the unseen process of our lives with others' polished results
believing that public success matters more than private happiness
expecting others to share their mistakes as openly as we do
items.exp: 부엌은 준비하고 실패도 하는 곳, 식당은 완성된 결과만 손님에게 보여 주는 곳이에요. 즉 밑줄 친 부분은 우리 삶의 지저분한 과정 전체를 남들의 다듬어진 결과와 비교하는 것을 뜻하므로 ③이 정답이에요. ②는 음식이라는 낱말만 빌린 오답이에요.

items.passage: Every autumn, jays in many forests collect thousands of acorns and bury them one by one in the soil. They do this to prepare for winter, when food becomes hard to find. A single bird may hide several thousand acorns in a season, spread over a wide area. Although jays have an impressive memory for their hiding places, they do not recover every acorn. Some are forgotten, and others are left behind when the bird finds enough food elsewhere. These leftover acorns are already planted at just the right depth, far from the shade of their parent tree. In spring, many of them sprout into young oaks. In this way, the birds' winter food supply turns into the start of a new forest. Scientists believe that jays have played a major role in helping oak forests spread across large areas, a job that the heavy acorns could never manage on their own.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the role of jays' food storage in spreading oak forests
the reasons jays have better memory than other birds
the difficulty oak trees face in growing under shade
the competition between jays and other animals for acorns
the effect of cold winters on the number of forest birds
items.exp: 어치가 겨울 대비로 묻어 둔 도토리 중 찾지 못한 것이 싹을 틔워 참나무 숲이 넓게 퍼진다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ①이 주제예요. 어치의 기억력이나 그늘은 일부 내용일 뿐 글 전체를 아우르지 못해요.

items.passage: Many people believe that photos stored on a computer or phone will last forever. After all, digital files do not fade or tear like paper prints. In reality, however, digital memories can be surprisingly fragile. Hard drives fail without warning, phones are lost or broken, and online services sometimes close and delete their users' data. Even when a file survives, the software needed to open it may disappear. Files saved in a format that was popular twenty years ago can be difficult to open today. A shoebox of old prints in the attic, by contrast, can still be enjoyed decades later with nothing more than a pair of eyes. This does not mean we should go back to film cameras. It means that digital photos need active care: copying them to more than one place, checking them every few years, and moving them to new formats when necessary.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How Film Cameras Are Making a Comeback
Why Paper Prints Fade Faster Than We Think
The Best Online Services for Sharing Photos
Digital Photos: Not as Permanent as They Seem
Smartphones Have Changed the Way We Take Pictures
items.exp: 디지털 사진은 영원할 것 같지만 기기 고장, 서비스 종료, 파일 형식 변화 때문에 쉽게 사라질 수 있어 적극적인 관리가 필요하다는 글이에요. 그래서 ④가 제목으로 알맞아요. 필름 카메라로 돌아가자는 뜻은 아니라고 했으므로 ①은 틀려요.

items.passage: Edith Valcourt (1868–1941) was a Canadian mapmaker known for her detailed maps of the northern lakes. She was born in a small town in Quebec, where her father worked as a land surveyor. As a child, she often went with him on trips and learned to use his measuring tools before she was twelve. Because women were not allowed to study surveying at the local college, she studied mathematics instead and taught at a girls' school for several years. In 1897, she joined a government team exploring the region north of Lake Superior, becoming the only woman on the team. Over the next fifteen years, she produced more than forty maps, many of which were used by railway builders. Later in life, she wrote a book for young readers about how maps are made. Her original drawings are now kept at a national museum in Ottawa.
items.q: 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 열두 살이 되기 전에 측량 도구 사용법을 배웠다.
1897년에 정부 탐사팀의 유일한 여성 대원이 되었다.
원본 지도 그림은 오타와의 국립 박물관에 보관되어 있다.
items.exp: 여성은 지역 대학에서 측량학을 공부할 수 없어서 대신 수학을 공부했다고 했으므로 ③이 글의 내용과 맞지 않아요. 나머지는 아버지의 직업, 열두 살 전의 경험, 1897년 탐사팀 합류, 오타와 박물관 보관 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage: When children play in a park without adults, they often spend a surprising amount of time arguing about the rules. Is the big tree a safe base? Does a ball that hits the fence still count? To an adult watching, these arguments may ①[seem] like a waste of playing time. Yet researchers who study play believe that this is where some of the most valuable learning takes place. To keep the game going, children must explain their views, listen to others, and find solutions ②[that] everyone can accept. A child who insists on unfair rules soon finds himself ③[left] out, because the others simply stop playing with him. Organized sports, ④[where] rules are fixed by adults and enforced by referees, offer fewer chances to practice these skills. Interestingly, the rules that children create on their own ⑤[is] often more respected than those handed down by adults.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: ⑤의 주어는 복수인 the rules이므로 is가 아니라 are가 되어야 해요(that children create on their own은 주어를 꾸미는 관계절이에요). ①은 조동사 may 뒤 동사원형, ②는 accept의 목적어 역할을 하는 관계대명사, ③은 find+목적어+과거분사, ④는 뒤에 완전한 절이 오는 관계부사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Laws affect everyone, yet many of them are written in language that only lawyers can understand. Long sentences, rare words, and phrases borrowed from Latin make legal documents ①[difficult] for ordinary people to read. Some lawyers argue that such wording is needed to make the law precise. However, studies of contracts and government forms show that clear, simple sentences are usually just as exact and far less likely to be ②[understood]. This matters because people can hardly obey a rule they cannot read. For this reason, several countries have passed laws that ③[require] government offices to write in plain language. The results have been encouraging. Citizens who can read a law for themselves are better able to ④[defend] their rights, and offices spend less time answering questions caused by simple ⑤[confusion]. A law, after all, is a message from a society to its members, and a message that cannot be understood has failed.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 쉽고 분명한 문장도 똑같이 정확하면서 훨씬 덜 오해받는다는 흐름이므로, ②의 understood는 misunderstood로 바꿔야 해요. 이해될 가능성이 훨씬 적다고 하면 쉬운 법률 언어를 지지하는 글의 내용과 반대가 돼요. 나머지 낱말은 문맥에 맞아요.

items.passage: Most people dislike waiting in line, but the length of the wait is often not what upsets us most. Many shoppers say they would rather stand for ten minutes in an orderly line than for five minutes in a line where someone cuts in ahead of them. What people really care about, it seems, is whether the line is ___. A queue is a small social agreement: whoever arrives first is served first, and everyone accepts a delay in exchange for that promise. When someone breaks the agreement, the extra minute it costs the others is tiny, yet their reaction can be surprisingly strong, because the rule itself has been insulted. This is also why many banks and airports use a single long line that feeds several counters. Such a line may not move any faster, but no one ends up stuck behind a slow customer while people who arrived later move ahead.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 사람들은 짧은 줄보다 아무도 새치기하지 않는 줄을 원하고, 먼저 온 사람이 먼저 서비스를 받는 약속이 깨질 때 화를 낸다고 했어요. 그러므로 빈칸에는 공정한(fair)이 알맞아요. 기다리는 시간의 길이는 가장 중요한 것이 아니라고 했으므로 ②, ⑤는 답이 아니에요.

items.passage: In most businesses, the goal is to defeat your competitors, and a company that drives every rival out of the market can make enormous profits. Professional sports leagues cannot work this way. Imagine a soccer club so rich that it buys every talented player and wins each match by ten goals. For a season or two, its fans might enjoy the victories. Soon, however, attendance would fall, even among its own supporters, because the very thing that makes sport worth watching, not knowing who will win, would have disappeared. A club's product, in other words, is not a victory but a contest, and a contest requires a worthy opponent. This is why many leagues limit how much each team can spend on players or let the weakest teams choose new players first. Such rules may look like charity toward the losers, but they reflect a basic fact of sporting life: ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: fans stay loyal only to the teams that win most often
a league is strongest when one club rules every season
talent matters less than money in deciding a match
even the best team depends on the survival of its rivals
players perform better when their salaries are limited
items.exp: 스포츠 구단이 파는 것은 승리가 아니라 승부이고, 승부에는 맞설 만한 상대가 필요하므로 리그가 약한 팀을 돕는 규칙을 둔다는 글이에요. 그래서 최강 팀도 경쟁자들이 살아남아야 존재할 수 있다는 ④가 알맞아요. ②는 한 팀이 독주하면 관중이 줄어든다는 내용과 반대이고, ③은 글에서 다루지 않은 비교예요.

items.passage: In many two-player games, the player who moves first has a small but real advantage, because he or she can begin carrying out a plan before the opponent has a chance to respond. ① In chess, for example, records of thousands of professional games show that White, which always moves first, wins noticeably more often than Black. ② Game designers and organizers have therefore looked for ways to make up for this unfairness. ③ Chess pieces were once carved from wood or bone, but today most sets are made of plastic because it is cheaper and lasts longer. ④ In the board game Go, the second player is given extra points, called komi, which are added to his or her final score. ⑤ The number of these points has been raised several times over the years, as players have learned how valuable the first move really is.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 글은 먼저 두는 사람의 이점과 그 불공평을 보완하는 방법(바둑의 덤)을 다루고 있어요. ③은 체스 말의 재료 변화에 관한 내용이라 선수의 이점과 관계가 없어요. ④와 ⑤는 ②에서 말한 보완 방법을 구체적으로 이어 가요.

items.passage:
On some mountainous islands and in deep valleys around the world, people developed an unusual way to talk across long distances: they whistled.

(A) These whistles are not simple signals that mean only "come here" or "danger." They are a form of the local spoken language, in which the rise and fall of the voice is turned into the rise and fall of a whistled tone.

(B) When roads and telephones arrived, however, that advantage disappeared, and fewer young people bothered to learn. To keep the tradition alive, some communities now teach whistled speech to children in their schools.

(C) Because the whistle follows speech itself, a skilled whistler can send a complete message, such as a request to bring water or news of a lost goat, to a listener more than a kilometer away. In steep places where crossing a valley on foot could take an hour, this was a great advantage.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 휘파람으로 말한다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 그 휘파람이 단순 신호가 아니라 말소리의 높낮이를 옮긴 언어라는 (A)가 와요. (C)는 휘파람이 말 자체를 따르기 때문에 완전한 메시지를 멀리 보낼 수 있다는 큰 장점(this was a great advantage)을 말하고, (B)는 도로와 전화가 생기며 that advantage가 사라졌다고 하므로 (A)-(C)-(B)예요.

items.passage: Most substances become denser when they change from a liquid to a solid, because their molecules pack more tightly together. A piece of solid wax, for example, sinks to the bottom of a pot of melted wax. ( ① ) Water, however, behaves differently. ( ② ) As it cools below about four degrees Celsius, its molecules begin to arrange themselves into an open pattern that takes up more space. ( ③ ) By the time water freezes, this pattern makes ice about nine percent less dense than liquid water, which is why ice floats. ( ④ ) If ice sank, lakes would freeze from the bottom up, and many of them could turn completely solid during a cold winter. ( ⑤ ) As a result, fish and other creatures can survive the winter in the liquid water beneath the ice.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

Instead, the ice stays on top, where it acts like a blanket that keeps the water below from losing heat.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 Instead는 '얼음이 가라앉으면 호수가 바닥부터 얼 것'이라는 가정과 실제 상황을 대조해요. 또 ⑤ 뒤의 As a result는 얼음이 담요처럼 열을 지켜 준 결과로 물고기가 살아남는다는 내용이므로 ⑤가 알맞아요. ④에 넣으면 앞 문장과 대조되는 내용이 없어 Instead가 어색해요.

items.passage: Imagine you visit a friend's home abroad and offer a small gift. Your friend politely says no. In many Western countries, you might take this answer at face value and put the gift away. In several Asian cultures, however, saying no to a gift once or even twice is considered good manners. Accepting immediately might make the receiver look greedy. The giver, who understands this custom, is expected to offer again, often insisting gently until the gift is finally taken. Both people know the first answer is part of a polite exchange rather than a real rejection. Problems arise when visitors who do not know the custom take that answer seriously. They may feel hurt, while their host may wonder why the gift was offered only once. Knowing the unspoken rules behind such small exchanges can prevent misunderstandings and help guests show respect.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In some cultures, a gift is often (A) ___ at first out of politeness, and the giver is expected to (B) ___ in offering it.
items.exp: 일부 아시아 문화에서는 선물을 한두 번 사양하는 것이 예의이고(A: refused), 주는 사람은 받을 때까지 부드럽게 계속 권해야 한다고 했어요(B: persist). 그래서 ②가 정답이에요. 바로 받으면 욕심 있어 보인다고 했으므로 accepted는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage:
Long before air conditioning was invented, people living in hot regions found clever ways to keep their homes cool. In many desert towns, houses were built with thick walls of mud or stone. These walls (a)[absorb] the sun's heat slowly during the day and release it at night, so the rooms inside stay comfortable even when the air outside is burning hot. Narrow streets kept buildings in each other's shade, and small windows reduced the amount of direct sunlight entering a room. Many homes also had a courtyard in the center, where trees and a small pool of water helped cool the air before it flowed into the surrounding rooms.

In the twentieth century, these lessons were largely (b)[forgotten]. Cheap energy made it possible to build glass towers almost anywhere and simply cool them with machines. Such buildings look the same whether they stand in a cold northern city or a tropical one. However, they come at a high cost. Large glass walls let in enormous amounts of heat, and the air conditioners needed to (c)[remove] it consume huge amounts of electricity.

Today, as energy prices rise and concerns about climate change grow, architects are turning back to traditional ideas. They are designing buildings with shaded windows, natural airflow, and walls that store heat. Some even include modern versions of the central courtyard. These features do not always replace air conditioning, but they greatly (d)[increase] the amount of energy a building needs. The wisdom of builders who worked without electricity, it turns out, may be (e)[essential] for the buildings of the future.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Old Solutions for Cooling Modern Buildings
Why Glass Towers Are Becoming More Popular
The History of the Air Conditioner
How Climate Change Damages Old Buildings
items.exp: 전기 없이 집을 시원하게 했던 전통 건축의 지혜를 오늘날 건축가들이 다시 활용하고 있다는 글이므로 ①이 제목으로 알맞아요. ④는 첫 문단 내용에만 해당하고, ②는 유리 건물의 문제점을 다룬 글의 흐름과 맞지 않아요.

items.exp: 그늘진 창, 자연 환기, 열을 저장하는 벽 같은 전통적 특징은 에어컨을 완전히 대신하지는 못해도 건물에 필요한 에너지를 크게 줄여 준다는 흐름이에요. 따라서 (d)의 increase를 reduce로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지 낱말은 문맥에 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Leo had been looking forward to the city's spring painting contest for months. The theme that year was "My Town," and he planned to paint the old clock tower in the town square. On the morning of the contest, he arrived at the park early with his paints, brushes, and a large sheet of paper. Hundreds of children were already setting up their easels under the tall cherry trees, chatting excitedly. When the signal was given, (a)[he] began sketching the tower carefully, line by line.

(B)
Just then, Mr. Grant, his art teacher, came over to see how his students were doing. He looked at the stains for a moment and then pointed at them. "What do these remind you of?" (b)[he] asked. Leo looked again. The gray shapes spread across the street like the puddles left after a spring shower on the old stone streets. Suddenly, Leo had an idea, and he picked up his brush again.

(C)
About an hour later, a sudden wind swept through the park. Leo's water cup tipped over, and dirty water ran across the bottom of his painting. Gray stains covered the street he had drawn so carefully. Leo stared at the ruined paper with tears in his eyes. There was not enough time to start again, and he wondered whether (c)[he] should simply pack up and go home.

(D)
Leo turned the stains into puddles that reflected the clock tower, and he added people with colorful umbrellas hurrying across the wet square. When (d)[he] finished, the painting looked as if it had been raining all along. Some of the judges stopped in front of it for a long time. That afternoon, the results were announced. His painting did not win first prize, but it received a special award for creativity. Holding the certificate, Leo searched the crowd until he found Mr. Grant, and (e)[he] ran over to thank his teacher.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: (A)에서 Leo가 시계탑을 그리기 시작하고, (C)에서 바람에 물이 쏟아져 얼룩이 생겨요. (B)에서 처음 등장하는 Mr. Grant가 그 얼룩(the stains)을 가리키며 아이디어를 주고, (D)에서 Leo가 얼룩을 물웅덩이로 바꿔 상을 받아요. 그래서 (C)-(B)-(D)예요.

items.exp: (D)에서 Leo의 그림은 1등상을 받지 못했지만 창의성 특별상을 받았다고 했으므로 ⑤가 글의 내용과 맞지 않아요. 나머지는 (A)의 주제와 계획, (C)의 바람, (D)의 우산 든 사람들 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage:
Dear Ms. Whitaker,

My name is Jenna Park, and I teach art at Eastfield High School. Every spring, my students study how famous painters used light and color, and this year we hope to learn directly from the works in your museum's European Gallery. I am writing to ask whether our class could be allowed to sketch in the gallery for two hours on the morning of Wednesday, April 14. I understand that drawing materials are usually not permitted inside the exhibition rooms. Our twenty-two students would use only pencils and small sketchbooks, with no paint, ink, or easels, and they would stay at least one meter away from every painting. Two teachers would be with them at all times to make sure they stay quiet and do not block other visitors. I would be grateful if you could let me know whether this is possible.

Sincerely,
Jenna Park
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 학생 미술 작품을 전시할 공간을 빌려 달라고 부탁하려고
전시실에서 학생들이 스케치할 수 있도록 허락을 요청하려고
전시실 안 그림 도구 반입 규정을 바꾸자고 건의하려고
유럽 회화 특별 강연의 강사를 초청하려고
items.exp: 필자는 미술 교사로서 학생들이 4월 14일 오전에 유럽 전시실에서 두 시간 동안 스케치할 수 있게 해 달라고 부탁하고, 연필만 쓰고 그림과 거리를 두겠다는 조건을 밝히고 있어요. 그래서 ③이 정답이에요. 규정 자체를 바꾸자는 것이 아니라 한 번의 허락을 구하는 글이므로 ④는 틀려요.

items.passage: For two whole weekends, Dan had worked on his kite in the garage. He had cut the thin wooden sticks himself, glued bright red paper over the frame, and tied a long tail of ribbons to the bottom. On Sunday morning, the wind was perfect, and he carried the kite up the hill behind his house, smiling all the way. "This is going to fly higher than anything in the neighborhood," he told his little sister. He held the string tightly and started running. The kite rose, wobbled for a second, and then turned sharply and dived straight into the grass. Dan tried again, and again, but each time it crashed after only a few meters. On the fourth try, one of the sticks snapped in half. Dan sat down on the wet grass and stared at the torn red paper. All that work, he thought, and it had not stayed in the air for even ten seconds.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Dan의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: Dan은 연을 들고 웃으며 언덕에 올라가 누구보다 높이 날 거라고 들떠 있었지만, 연이 계속 추락하고 살대까지 부러지자 젖은 풀밭에 주저앉아요. 그래서 들뜸에서 실망으로 바뀐 ①이 정답이에요. 처음에 겁을 먹거나 짜증이 난 상태가 아니었으므로 ②, ⑤는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Many of us find it hard to say no. A friend asks for help with a project, a club needs another volunteer, a classmate wants to meet after school, and we agree to all of it. Each request seems small, and saying yes feels kind. The problem is that our time does not grow to match our promises. An afternoon has the same number of hours no matter how many things we put into it. When we agree to one thing, we are quietly choosing not to do something else, whether it is studying, resting, or spending time with family. In this sense, every yes is like [spending a coin you can only spend once]. Before we reach into our pocket, it is worth asking what else that coin could have bought. Saying no is not always selfish; sometimes it is the only way to protect the things that matter most to us.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [spending a coin you can only spend once]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: refusing to share what we own with other people
giving up other uses of our limited time by agreeing
saving our energy for the most difficult tasks first
expecting a reward every time we help someone
trying to please everyone in order to be popular
items.exp: 우리의 시간은 약속에 맞춰 늘어나지 않으므로, 한 가지에 동의하면 공부나 휴식 같은 다른 일을 포기하게 된다고 했어요. 즉 한 번만 쓸 수 있는 동전을 쓴다는 것은 제한된 시간의 다른 쓰임을 포기한다는 뜻이므로 ②가 정답이에요. ①은 거절의 뜻이라 반대이고, ④는 보상 이야기가 없어 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Online stores often offer free delivery on orders over a certain amount, such as thirty dollars. This seems like a simple gift to customers, but it has a powerful effect on how they shop. Suppose your cart contains items worth twenty-six dollars, and delivery costs five dollars. Instead of paying the fee, many shoppers search for something small to add, even if they did not plan to buy it. They often end up spending more than the delivery fee would have cost. What makes this happen is not careful calculation but the strong attraction of the word "free." Paying nothing for delivery feels like winning, while paying a fee feels like a loss, even when the numbers say otherwise. Stores understand this feeling well and set their limits just above the amount that most customers usually spend. The free delivery offer, in other words, is designed less to save customers money than to increase what they spend.
items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 온라인 쇼핑은 오프라인 쇼핑보다 비용이 적게 든다.
배송비는 상품의 무게와 거리에 따라 정해져야 한다.
소비자는 필요한 물건을 미리 목록으로 정리해야 한다.
무료 배송 기준은 소비자의 지출을 늘리도록 고안된 것이다.
무료 배송은 상점이 손해를 보면서 제공하는 서비스이다.
items.exp: 무료 배송이라는 말의 매력 때문에 소비자가 배송비보다 더 많은 돈을 쓰게 되며, 상점은 이를 노리고 기준 금액을 정한다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ④가 요지예요. 상점이 손해를 본다는 ⑤는 글의 마지막 문장과 반대예요.

items.passage: An octopus resting on a rock can suddenly seem to disappear. Within less than a second, its skin may change from bright orange to the gray and brown of the stone beneath it. This remarkable ability comes from thousands of tiny color cells just under the skin. Each cell contains a small sac of colored pigment surrounded by muscles. When the muscles pull, the sac stretches and the color spreads out; when they relax, the color shrinks into a tiny dot. Because these cells are controlled directly by nerves, the octopus can change them far faster than animals that rely on slower chemical signals. Some species can also raise small bumps on their skin to copy the rough texture of coral or seaweed. Together, these tools allow the octopus to hide from predators, sneak up on prey, and even flash warning patterns when it feels threatened.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the dangers octopuses face from predators in the ocean
the reasons octopuses prefer to live on rocks and coral
the differences between octopuses and other sea animals
the role of chemical signals in animal communication
how octopuses quickly change their appearance to survive
items.exp: 문어가 신경으로 직접 조절되는 색소 세포와 피부 돌기를 이용해 순식간에 몸 색과 질감을 바꾸어 숨거나 사냥한다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ⑤가 주제예요. 화학 신호는 문어와 비교하기 위해 잠깐 나온 내용이라 ④는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Two charts can show exactly the same numbers and still tell very different stories. Imagine that a school's reading club had 50 members last year and 54 this year. If the bars on a chart begin at zero, the second bar looks only slightly taller than the first, which is an honest picture of a small increase. But if the line of numbers on the left side starts at 48 instead of zero, the second bar suddenly looks three times as tall as the first. Nothing in the data has changed, yet a reader who only glances at the chart may believe that membership has nearly tripled. Some advertisers use this trick on purpose, while other people do it by accident because their software chooses the starting point automatically. Either way, the lesson is simple: before you react to the height of a bar, look at the numbers along its side.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Make a Chart with Free Software
Why Reading Clubs Are Growing So Fast
Read the Side Before You Trust the Bars
Honest Advertisers Always Use Bar Charts
Small Increases Are Not Worth Reporting
items.exp: 같은 자료라도 그래프 세로축이 0이 아닌 48에서 시작하면 작은 증가가 세 배처럼 보인다며, 막대 높이를 믿기 전에 옆의 숫자를 확인하라고 말하는 글이에요. 그래서 ③이 제목으로 알맞아요. ②는 예로 든 독서 동아리 내용만 빌린 오답이에요.

items.passage:
Harbor City Junior Coding Camp 2027

Spend five exciting days learning to build your own games and apps! No experience is needed.

• Who: Students aged 12 to 16
• Fee: $120 per person ($100 for Science Center members)

Program

Notes

• Lunch is not included. Please bring your own lunch.
