items.passage:
Dear Residents of Sunhill Apartments,

Over the past few months, the number of pigeons around Building B has grown quickly. Some residents have kindly been leaving bread and rice for them near the playground and the main entrance. We understand that these neighbors care about the birds, but the food has also brought problems. Pigeon droppings now cover the benches and the slide, and parents have told us that they no longer feel comfortable letting their children play there. Leftover food also attracts rats at night, and the cleaning staff spend over an hour each morning washing the area. For these reasons, we ask all residents to stop feeding pigeons anywhere on the apartment grounds, starting this Monday. We will put up new signs and clean the playground thoroughly this weekend. Thank you for helping us keep our shared spaces clean and safe for everyone.

Sincerely,
Minsu Park
Building Manager
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 청소 직원 추가 채용 계획을 알리려고
쥐 퇴치 방법에 대한 의견을 구하려고
단지 안에서 비둘기에게 먹이를 주지 말아 달라고 요청하려고
새 안내판 설치 비용의 분담을 부탁하려고
items.exp: 비둘기에게 먹이를 주면서 놀이터가 더러워지고 쥐가 꼬인다고 설명한 뒤, 이번 월요일부터 단지 어디에서도 먹이를 주지 말아 달라(stop feeding pigeons)고 요청하고 있어요. 그래서 ④가 알맞아요. 안내판 설치와 청소는 관리실이 할 일을 알린 부분이에요.

items.passage: Every Sunday, Yerin's grandfather called her from his small town far away, but he could only hear her voice. This week she had decided to teach him how to make a video call. "Press the green button with the camera on it," she said slowly. "Which camera?" he asked. For twenty minutes, he pressed the wrong buttons, turned off his phone twice, and once called his neighbor by mistake. Yerin rubbed her forehead and let out a long sigh. She wanted to give up and simply talk on the phone as usual. "Let's try one last time, Grandpa," she said, and she explained each step again, even more slowly. Suddenly, her screen flickered, and there was her grandfather's face, a little too close to the camera, grinning widely. "I can see you!" he shouted. Yerin laughed and leaned back in her chair. All that patience had been worth it, and she felt proud of both of them.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Yerin의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 할아버지가 계속 엉뚱한 버튼을 누르자 Yerin은 이마를 문지르며 한숨을 쉬고 포기하고 싶어 했어요. 마침내 화면에 할아버지 얼굴이 나타나자 웃으며 인내한 보람을 느끼고 뿌듯해했으므로 frustrated → satisfied가 알맞아요.

items.passage: Imagine a garden with both flowers and weeds. If you spend all your time and water on the weeds, they will grow tall and strong while the flowers slowly die. Our minds work in a similar way. Each day brings small annoyances: a rude comment, a bus that arrives late, a mistake at school. If we replay these moments again and again in our heads, they begin to take up more space than they deserve. Before long, an ordinary day full of pleasant moments feels like a bad one. On the other hand, when we choose to notice what went well, such as a friend's joke or a delicious lunch, those memories become stronger and easier to recall. We cannot stop every unpleasant thing from happening. However, we can stop [watering the weeds] and give our attention to the flowers instead.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [watering the weeds]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: avoiding people who often make rude comments
taking care of plants that are hard to grow
focusing our thoughts on small negative events
trying to fix every mistake as soon as possible
ignoring problems that need to be solved
items.exp: 작은 불쾌한 일들을 머릿속에서 계속 되새기면 그것들이 실제보다 큰 자리를 차지한다고 했어요. 따라서 잡초에 물을 주는 것은 사소한 부정적 일에 생각을 집중하는 것을 뜻해요. ⑤는 해결할 문제를 무시한다는 뜻이라 글의 맥락과 달라요.

items.passage: Many parents worry when their children choose comic books or simple adventure stories instead of the classics on a school reading list. They fear that such books are a waste of time. However, the books that build strong readers are often the ones that children pick up on their own and cannot put down. When young people read for pleasure, they read more pages, more often, and for longer periods. Along the way, they meet thousands of new words in natural contexts and learn their meanings without looking them up. They also develop the habit of reading, which makes it easier to handle more difficult texts later. A child who reads ten comic books with excitement may gain more than one who struggles through a single classic out of duty. Therefore, it is wiser to protect children's joy in reading than to control every book they choose.
items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 고전 문학은 어린 시절에 읽어야 그 가치를 이해할 수 있다.
만화책은 아이들의 어휘력 향상에 방해가 된다.
아이들이 즐겁게 스스로 고른 책을 읽는 것이 독서 능력을 키운다.
부모는 아이와 함께 책을 읽는 시간을 정해야 한다.
어려운 글을 읽을 때는 사전을 활용하는 습관이 필요하다.
items.exp: 아이들이 스스로 골라 즐겁게 읽는 책이 더 많이, 더 자주 읽게 하여 어휘와 독서 습관을 길러 준다는 내용이에요. ②는 만화책이 어휘력에 방해가 된다는 것으로 글과 반대예요.

items.passage: In autumn, the leaves of many trees turn yellow and red before falling to the ground. This may look like a sign of weakness, but it is actually a clever survival plan. In winter, the ground freezes, and roots can hardly take in water. Broad leaves, however, constantly lose water into the air through tiny holes on their surface. If a tree kept its leaves all winter, it would dry out like a towel hanging in the wind. Heavy snow resting on wide leaves could also break branches. So, as the days grow shorter, the tree pulls useful nutrients from its leaves back into its branches and roots, where they are stored for spring. Then it seals off each leaf at its base, and the leaf drops. By letting go of its leaves, the tree saves water, protects its branches, and keeps the resources it needs to grow again.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the beauty of colorful autumn leaves
why trees drop their leaves before winter
how roots absorb water from frozen ground
the damage heavy snow causes to forests
ways to protect garden trees in cold weather
items.exp: 나무가 겨울 전에 잎을 떨어뜨리는 이유(수분 손실 방지, 가지 보호, 양분 저장)를 설명하는 글이에요. ④의 눈 피해는 이유 중 하나로만 언급되어 주제로는 너무 좁아요.

items.passage: Elephants are famous for their loud trumpeting, but much of their conversation is something we cannot hear at all. They also produce deep rumbles that are too low in pitch for human ears. These low sounds travel much farther than high ones, because they are not easily blocked by trees or tall grass. As a result, an elephant can send a message to family members several kilometers away. The rumbles also travel through the ground. Scientists believe that elephants can pick up these vibrations through their sensitive feet and trunks, sometimes lifting one foot off the ground as if listening. In this way, a mother can call a lost calf, or a herd can warn others that danger is near. Researchers have even found that elephants respond differently to the rumbles of family members than to those of strangers. What sounds like silence to us may actually be a busy conversation.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How Elephants Use Their Trunks to Find Water
The Danger of Human Noise for Wild Elephants
Talking Below Our Hearing: The Elephant's Hidden Voice
Why Elephant Calves Often Get Lost
items.exp: 코끼리가 사람이 듣지 못하는 낮은 소리로 먼 곳의 가족과 소통하고, 발과 코로 땅의 진동까지 느낀다는 내용이라 ④가 알맞아요. ①은 첫 문장에서 대조로만 언급된 트럼펫 소리를 빌린 오답이에요.

items.passage:
Harborview Kids Cooking Camp 2027

Let your kids discover the fun of cooking! Our chefs will teach simple, healthy recipes from around the world.

Notes

items.q: Harborview Kids Cooking Camp 2027에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 아이들은 직접 만든 요리를 점심으로 먹는다.
items.exp: 6월 30일 이전에 등록해야 100달러로 할인을 받을 수 있어요(for registrations before June 30). 그래서 ③이 안내문과 일치하지 않아요.

items.passage: On a cold morning, a metal door handle feels much colder than a wooden door, even though both have been in the same room all night and ①[are] actually at the same temperature. Why does this happen? The answer is that our skin does not measure temperature directly. Instead, it senses how fast heat ②[leave] our body. Metal is a good conductor, which means it carries heat away from your hand very quickly. Wood, on the other hand, is a poor conductor, so heat moves into it slowly and stays near the surface ③[touching] your skin. As a result, the metal draws more warmth from your fingers and ④[makes] them feel cold. This is also why a tile floor feels colder under bare feet than a carpet ⑤[does]. Both floors may be equally cool, but the tile takes your body heat away much faster.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: ②는 간접의문문 how fast 뒤의 주어가 단수 heat이므로 leave를 leaves로 고쳐야 해요. ①은 주어 both에 맞는 복수 동사, ③은 the surface를 꾸미는 현재분사, ④는 draws와 병렬인 단수 동사, ⑤는 feels cold를 대신하는 대동사라 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: The square black-and-white patterns called QR codes appear on everything from posters to restaurant menus. A phone camera can read one in less than a second, even when part of the code is ①[damaged] or dirty. This is possible because the code does not store each piece of information only once. Instead, it includes extra data that ②[repeats] the message in a mathematical form. If some squares cannot be read, the phone uses this extra data to ③[rebuild] the missing parts. Some QR codes can still work with nearly a third of their surface ④[covered]. This is why companies sometimes place a small logo in the middle of a code without making it unreadable. The extra data does make the code larger and more crowded, but most designers agree that this is a small price to pay for ⑤[weakness].
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: QR 코드는 여분의 데이터 덕분에 일부가 손상되거나 가려져도 읽힌다는 내용이에요. 코드가 커지는 것은 그런 튼튼함을 얻기 위한 작은 대가이므로 ⑤의 weakness를 reliability 같은 낱말로 바꿔야 해요.

items.passage: Noise-canceling headphones can make a noisy airplane cabin feel almost silent. Surprisingly, they do this not by blocking sound but by adding more of it. Sound travels as waves, with high points and low points. A tiny microphone on the outside of the headphones constantly listens to the noise around you, such as the hum of an engine. A small computer chip then quickly creates a new sound wave that is the exact ___ of the incoming noise: where the noise has a high point, the new wave has a low point, and where the noise has a low point, the new wave has a high point. When the two waves meet inside your ear, they cancel each other out. The result is that the steady roar of the engine nearly disappears, while you can still enjoy your music.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 새로 만든 음파는 소음이 높은 곳에서 낮고, 낮은 곳에서 높다고 했으므로 소음의 정반대인 opposite이 알맞아요. copy나 echo는 같은 모양의 파동이라 소음을 오히려 키우게 되어 답이 아니에요.

items.passage: When a friend asks whether she should quit a club she no longer enjoys, the answer often seems obvious to us. Yet when we face the same kind of decision ourselves, we may hesitate for weeks. Why are we so much wiser about other people's problems? Part of the reason is that our own situations are full of details that pull our attention in different directions: the people we might disappoint, the time we have already spent, the fear of regret. Looking at a friend's problem, we do not feel these details as strongly, so we can focus on what matters most. Researchers have found that people reason more wisely about their own troubles when they imagine the situation as if it were happening to someone else. The lesson is not that we should care less about our own lives, but that a little ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: honesty about our feelings always leads to the right answer
help from others is necessary for every decision we make
more information makes any problem easier to solve
distance from a problem can make our thinking clearer
time spent alone helps us forget difficult choices
items.exp: 자기 문제는 여러 세부 사항에 마음이 흔들리지만 친구 문제는 한 걸음 떨어져 보기 때문에 중요한 것에 집중할 수 있다고 했어요. 자기 상황도 남의 일처럼 상상하면 더 현명해진다고 했으므로 ④가 알맞아요. ③은 오히려 세부 사항이 많아서 판단이 흐려진다는 글과 반대예요.

items.passage: Sometimes the best way to solve a problem is to change how people experience it rather than the problem itself. In the early days of tall office buildings, many workers complained that the elevators were too slow. ① Building owners first considered installing faster elevators, but that would have been very expensive and taken a long time. ② Then someone suggested a much cheaper solution: placing large mirrors next to the elevator doors. ③ While waiting, people checked their hair, straightened their clothes, or quietly watched others, and the time seemed to pass more quickly. ④ Complaints dropped sharply, even though the elevators moved at exactly the same speed as before. ⑤ Today, elevators in some of the world's tallest buildings can travel faster than sixty kilometers per hour.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 문제 자체가 아니라 사람들이 그것을 느끼는 방식을 바꿔 해결한 예로 엘리베이터 옆 거울을 소개하는 글이에요. ⑤는 오늘날 엘리베이터의 속도에 관한 내용이라, 속도는 그대로 두고 기다림의 느낌을 바꿨다는 흐름에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
We usually say that a year has 365 days. However, the Earth actually takes about 365 and a quarter days to travel once around the Sun.

(A) Even this correction is not perfect, because the extra time is actually a little less than a quarter of a day. So years ending in 00 are leap years only if they can be divided by 400, which is why 2000 was a leap year but 1900 was not.

(B) To prevent this, an extra day, February 29, is added to the calendar every fourth year. These years of 366 days are called leap years.

(C) This extra quarter of a day may seem too small to matter. Yet if it were ignored, the calendar would slip by about one day every four years, and after a few centuries, the seasons would no longer match the months.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 1년이 실제로는 약 365와 4분의 1일이라는 주어진 글 다음에, 이 남는 4분의 1일(This extra quarter of a day)을 무시하면 달력이 밀린다는 (C)가 와요. (B)의 To prevent this가 (C)의 달력이 밀리는 문제를 받아 윤년을 소개하고, (A)의 this correction이 (B)의 윤년 규칙을 가리켜요.

items.passage: Imagine that you need help painting your room but cannot afford to pay a painter. In some communities, people solve this problem by trading their time instead of money through a system called a time bank. ( ① ) The idea is simple: for every hour you spend helping someone, you earn one hour of credit. ( ② ) You can then spend that credit to receive an hour of help from any other member. ( ③ ) What makes time banks special is that everyone's hour is worth exactly the same. ( ④ ) This may sound unfair to some, since the lawyer has spent years in training. ( ⑤ ) However, the rule sends a powerful message that every person has something useful to offer. Retired people, students, and those without jobs can all feel valued as active members of the community. In this way, a time bank does more than exchange services; it builds trust among neighbors who might otherwise never have met. Many members say that the friendships they make are worth even more than the help they receive.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

An hour of legal advice from a lawyer, for example, earns the same credit as an hour spent walking a neighbor's dog.
items.exp: 주어진 문장은 모든 사람의 한 시간이 똑같은 가치라는 원칙의 예시(for example)이므로 그 바로 뒤인 ④에 들어가요. ④ 뒤의 This may sound unfair와 the lawyer가 주어진 문장의 변호사 예시를 가리키므로, 주어진 문장이 없으면 연결이 끊겨요.

items.passage: Paying with a card or a phone feels quick and easy, but it may also change how much we spend. When people pay with cash, they physically hand over bills and watch their wallets become thinner. This creates a small but real feeling of discomfort, which makes them think twice before buying. With a tap of a card, however, the money seems to disappear without any visible loss. In one study, shoppers who paid by card were willing to spend considerably more on the same items than those who paid with cash. Researchers suggest that this is because the 'pain of paying' is weaker when we cannot see the money leave our hands. So, if you want to control your spending, you might try leaving your card at home and carrying only the cash you plan to use.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

People tend to spend more when paying by card because they feel less (A) ___ when the money they give up is not (B) ___.
items.exp: 현금을 낼 때는 돈이 줄어드는 것을 보며 불편함을 느끼지만, 카드는 돈이 눈에 보이지 않게 빠져나가 '지불의 고통'이 약하다고 했어요. 그래서 (A)는 discomfort, (B)는 visible이 알맞아요.

items.passage:
For most of history, ordinary workers did not have weekends. In the early factories of the nineteenth century, many people worked six days a week, often twelve hours a day, and rested only on Sunday, which was mostly kept for religion. Free time was (a)[rare], and few workers had the energy to enjoy it.

Things began to change slowly. Some factory owners in Britain allowed workers to stop at noon on Saturday, partly because so many workers were (b)[absent] on Mondays after their single day off. In 1926, an American car maker went further and gave its workers both Saturday and Sunday off without lowering their weekly pay. Many people expected production to fall, but the company found that rested workers did better work. The two-day weekend soon (c)[spread] to other industries and countries.

The weekend also changed how people lived. With two free days, families could take short trips, play sports, or watch games together. Whole industries, from cinemas to amusement parks, grew because people finally had time to (d)[spend]. In this sense, the weekend was not only a gift to workers but also a boost to the economy.

Today, some companies are experimenting with a four-day working week. Supporters argue that, just as in 1926, extra rest can make people happier and more productive. Critics worry about costs and fairness. Whatever happens, the history of the weekend reminds us that rest is not simply time taken away from work. It can be what makes good work (e)[impossible].
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How the Weekend Was Born and Why Rest Matters
Why Factories Moved to Big Cities
The Dangers of Working Too Little
Sunday: A Day for Religion Only
items.exp: 하루만 쉬던 노동자에게 주말이 생겨난 과정과 주말이 삶과 경제를 바꾼 모습, 그리고 휴식이 좋은 일을 가능하게 한다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ①이 제목으로 알맞아요. ⑤는 주말 덕분에 생긴 여가의 한 예만 다룬 오답이에요.

items.exp: 휴식은 일에서 빼앗긴 시간이 아니라 좋은 일을 가능하게 하는 것이라는 흐름이므로 (e) impossible은 possible로 바꿔야 해요. (b) absent는 하루만 쉬고 난 월요일에 결근하는 노동자가 많았다는 뜻으로 알맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Every Saturday morning, Yuna volunteered at Sunrise Children's Hospital. Her job was simple: she pushed a cart full of books and games from room to room. On her first day, a nurse named Mrs. Kang led her to Room 304. "This is Leo," she said. "He's been here for three weeks, and he hasn't said much to anyone." A small boy with a cast on his leg was staring at the window. Yuna offered him a book, but (a)[he] shook his head without looking at her.

(B)
Over the next few weeks, the boy's drawings filled a whole notebook. One showed a dragon flying over the hospital, carrying children home. Mrs. Kang said that he had begun talking to the other patients and even laughing with the nurses. One Saturday, Yuna arrived to find Room 304 empty. Her heart sank until Mrs. Kang handed her an envelope. "Leo went home yesterday," (b)[she] said. "He asked me to give you this."

(C)
Inside the envelope was a drawing of a girl pushing a cart full of books. Above it, (c)[he] had written in large letters, "Thank you for coming back every week." Yuna stood still in the hallway, holding the paper carefully. She had come to the hospital to help others, but she realized that she had received something precious in return. That evening, she pinned the drawing above her desk, where it still hangs today.

(D)
The next Saturday, Yuna tried something different. Instead of books, she brought a box of colored pencils and a sketchbook. Without saying a word, she sat down and began to draw a cat. After a while, Leo turned his head. Yuna slid the sketchbook toward him, and slowly (d)[he] picked up a pencil. He added a long tail and a pair of wings to the cat. Yuna laughed, and for the first time, Leo smiled. When she left that day, (e)[he] said quietly, "Will you come next week?"
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: (A)에서 Leo가 책을 거절한 뒤, 다음 토요일에 그림 도구를 가져가 마음을 연 (D)가 와요. 몇 주 동안 그림이 쌓이고 Leo가 퇴원하며 봉투를 남긴 (B)가 이어지고, 봉투 속 그림을 보는 (C)로 끝나요.

items.passage:
Dear Residents of Maple Court,

My name is Daniel Shin, and I chair the residents' committee of our apartment complex. As many of you know, the rooftop of Building C has been empty for years. Last month, the committee voted to turn this space into a shared vegetable garden, and the building manager has already installed twenty raised planting boxes and a water tap. Now we need gardeners to fill them. Any resident may apply for one box, which can be used from April to November at no cost. Gardeners are simply asked to water their plants regularly and to help clean the shared tools once a month. If you would like a box, please fill out the form at the management office by March 20. Boxes will be given out in the order applications are received. We look forward to seeing the rooftop turn green.

Sincerely,
Daniel Shin
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 옥상 정원 조성 공사 일정을 알리려고
옥상 텃밭 상자 사용 신청을 안내하려고
공동 원예 도구 청소 당번을 정하려고
주민 위원회 회의 결과에 대한 의견을 구하려고
items.exp: 옥상에 텃밭 상자가 설치되었으니 원하는 주민은 3월 20일까지 관리사무소에서 신청서를 작성하라고 안내하고 있어요. 공사는 이미 끝났고 도구 청소는 참여 조건일 뿐이라 ①, ③은 목적이 아니에요.

items.passage: All night, the wind howled and rain beat against the windows. Hana lay awake, thinking about the three tomato plants on the balcony. She had grown them from tiny seeds since March, watering them every morning before school, and the first green tomatoes had finally appeared last week. Each time a strong gust rattled the glass, she pictured the thin stems snapping and the pots crashing to the floor. She pulled the blanket over her head, but she could not stop worrying. When the gray light of morning came, she hurried to the balcony door, afraid of what she would see. The pots had tipped over, and soil was scattered everywhere. But the plants themselves were still whole, their stems bent but unbroken, and the little tomatoes were still hanging on. Hana let out a long breath and smiled as she carefully set the pots upright again.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Hana의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 밤새 폭풍에 토마토 줄기가 부러질까 걱정하며 잠들지 못하던 Hana가, 아침에 화분은 넘어졌어도 식물과 열매가 무사한 것을 보고 긴 숨을 내쉬며 미소 지어요. 그래서 불안했다가 안도하는 심경으로 바뀌어요.

items.passage: Many parents feel guilty when their children say, "I'm bored." They rush to fill every empty hour with classes, screens, or planned activities. But boredom is not a problem that adults must always solve. In fact, it can be a valuable starting point. When children have nothing to do, they are pushed to look around and invent something on their own. A cardboard box becomes a spaceship, and a rainy afternoon turns into a day for drawing a comic book. These moments teach children to manage their own time and to discover what truly interests them. If adults step in too quickly, children learn that someone else is responsible for keeping them entertained. So the next time your child complains of having nothing to do, resist the urge to offer a solution. Give them a little space, and let their boredom do its quiet work.
items.q: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 아이가 지루함을 스스로 해결하도록 기다려 주어야 한다.
아이의 여가 시간을 다양한 활동으로 계획해 주어야 한다.
아이가 화면을 보는 시간을 엄격하게 제한해야 한다.
아이에게 시간 관리 방법을 직접 가르쳐야 한다.
아이의 관심사를 일찍 발견해 전문 교육을 시켜야 한다.
items.exp: 아이가 심심하다고 할 때 해결책을 주고 싶은 마음을 참고 지루함이 제 역할을 하게 두라고 마지막 부분에서 주장하고 있어요. ②는 필자가 비판하는 부모의 행동이에요.

items.passage: Many students meet Shakespeare for the first time in a classroom, where his plays are read slowly, line by line, with notes explaining every difficult word. It is easy to conclude from this experience that his works were meant to be serious, difficult art for educated readers. But in his own time, a trip to the theater was closer to going to a football match. Thousands of ordinary Londoners paid a penny to stand in the open yard in front of the stage. They ate snacks, cheered for heroes, shouted at villains, and laughed loudly at jokes, many of which were rude. Shakespeare knew his audience well. He filled his plays with sword fights, ghosts, and clowns to keep the crowd from getting bored. In short, [he wrote for the crowd, not for the classroom]. Remembering this can help us enjoy his plays as lively entertainment rather than as a difficult duty.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [he wrote for the crowd, not for the classroom]이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: He preferred writing poems to writing plays for the theater.
He wanted his plays to be studied carefully by future students.
He created his plays as popular entertainment for ordinary people.
He refused to perform his plays for wealthy and educated people.
He wrote his plays mainly to teach the public about history.
items.exp: 셰익스피어 시대의 관객은 한 페니를 내고 서서 먹고 소리치며 즐기던 평범한 런던 사람들이었고, 그는 칼싸움과 유령, 광대로 그들을 즐겁게 했어요. 그러니 밑줄은 그의 연극이 공부용이 아닌 대중의 오락으로 만들어졌다는 뜻이에요. ②는 교실을 위해 썼다는 것이라 정반대예요.

items.passage: Many online services offer a free month to new users. At first glance, this looks like a generous gift. Companies, however, know something about human behavior that makes these offers profitable. To start a free trial, customers usually have to enter their card details, and the subscription renews automatically once the trial ends. Canceling requires the customer to remember the date, find the right page, and click through several screens. Most people sincerely plan to cancel if they don't enjoy the service, but life gets busy, and the deadline passes quietly. Studies of subscription businesses suggest that many trial users end up paying for at least one month they never meant to buy. In other words, this business model depends less on how much customers love the product and more on the simple fact that doing nothing is easier than doing something.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: reasons customers prefer monthly payments to yearly ones
ways online services improve the quality of their products
the risk of sharing card details on unsafe websites
the growing number of people canceling online subscriptions
how free trials make money from customers' failure to act
items.exp: 무료 체험은 자동 갱신되고 해지가 번거로워, 해지하려던 사람들도 아무것도 하지 않아 결국 돈을 내게 된다는 내용이에요. 카드 정보 입력은 과정의 일부일 뿐 보안 위험을 다루지 않아 ③은 답이 아니에요.

items.passage: When you watch a movie, you are actually looking at a series of still pictures shown so quickly that your brain sees smooth movement. In the early days of film, there was no fixed speed for this. Cameras were often turned by hand, and silent films were usually shot at around 16 to 20 pictures, or frames, per second. Theaters sometimes even played films faster than they had been shot in order to fit more shows into an evening. This changed in the late 1920s, when sound arrived. Because the sound was recorded alongside the pictures, any change in speed would make voices sound strange, so the speed had to stay exactly the same. The industry settled on 24 frames per second. It was fast enough for clear sound and smooth movement, but slow enough to avoid wasting expensive film. Almost a century later, most movies are still made at this speed.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How Hand-Turned Cameras Created Movie Stars
Why Movies Settled on 24 Frames per Second
Silent Films: Faster Than They Should Be
The High Cost of Film in Early Hollywood
How Our Brains Turn Pictures into Sound
items.exp: 속도가 제각각이던 무성 영화 시대를 지나, 소리가 들어오면서 속도를 고정해야 했고 소리 품질과 필름 비용을 함께 고려해 초당 24장으로 정해졌다는 내용이므로 ②가 알맞아요. ③과 ④는 글의 일부 내용만 다뤄요.

items.passage: Nora Kilbride (1879–1958) was an Irish puppet maker whose wooden puppets delighted audiences across Europe. She was born in Galway, where her mother ran a small bookshop. As a girl, she loved making little figures out of cloth and acting out the stories she read in the shop. At seventeen, she moved to Dublin to study woodcarving, and soon she began working as an assistant in a furniture workshop. In 1908, she founded a traveling puppet theater with two former classmates. Unlike many puppet shows of her time, hers told stories about ordinary people, such as fishermen and farmers, rather than kings and knights. Her best-known show, a play about the four seasons of a fishing village, was first performed in 1931. In her later years, she taught puppet-making to young artists, and she kept carving until she was nearly eighty.
items.q: 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 열일곱 살에 목공예를 공부하러 더블린으로 갔다.
1908년에 옛 동창 두 명과 함께 순회 인형극단을 세웠다.
평범한 사람들보다 왕과 기사에 관한 이야기를 주로 다뤘다.
items.exp: 그녀의 인형극은 당시 많은 공연과 달리 왕과 기사보다 어부나 농부 같은 평범한 사람들의 이야기를 다뤘어요. 그래서 ④가 글과 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 모두 글의 내용과 같아요.

items.passage: Sloths are famous for being slow, but their slowness is a clever survival strategy. Their diet consists mainly of leaves, which ①[provide] very little energy and take a long time to digest. To live on such poor food, sloths have developed a body that uses energy as carefully as possible. Their muscles are much smaller than ②[those] of other animals of similar size, and their body temperature changes with the air around them. A sloth may move only a few dozen meters in a whole day, ③[spend] most of its time hanging quietly from a branch. This lack of movement also helps protect it from predators such as eagles, which hunt by spotting motion. In fact, sloths move so little that tiny green algae grow in their fur, ④[making] them even harder to see among the leaves. What looks like laziness, then, is actually a lifestyle ⑤[that] has kept sloths alive for millions of years.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: ③은 앞 절에 동사 may move가 이미 있으므로, 동시 상황을 나타내는 분사구문 spending으로 고쳐야 해요. ①은 선행사 leaves에 맞춘 복수 동사, ②는 muscles를 받는 those, ④는 결과의 분사구문, ⑤는 주격 관계대명사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Surgeons once wore white, like most doctors. In the early twentieth century, however, many hospitals switched to green or blue for operating rooms, and the reason has to do with how our eyes ①[work]. During an operation, a surgeon stares at red blood and tissue for long periods. When the eyes focus on one color for a long time, they become less ②[sensitive] to it. Then, if the surgeon looks up at a white wall or coat, a ghostly green image of what he or she was just looking at can appear. This "afterimage" can be ③[distracting] at a moment when full attention is needed. Green and blue, however, are opposite to red on the color wheel, so they help the eyes ④[recover] their balance, and any afterimage simply blends into the background. In addition, these colors make red details easier to see. In this way, a simple choice of color helps make surgery ⑤[riskier].
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 초록과 파랑이 잔상을 없애 주고 붉은 부분을 더 잘 보이게 하므로 색 선택이 수술을 더 안전하게 만든다는 흐름이에요. 따라서 ⑤ riskier를 safer로 바꿔야 해요. ②는 한 색을 오래 보면 그 색에 덜 민감해진다는 뜻이라 맞아요.

items.passage: Have you ever noticed how quiet the world becomes after a heavy snowfall? The streets seem hushed, and even the noise of distant traffic almost disappears. This is not just your imagination. Freshly fallen snow is made of countless tiny ice crystals that pile up loosely, leaving many small pockets of air between them. When sound waves enter the snow, they bounce around inside these pockets and gradually lose their energy instead of being reflected back into the air. In this way, a layer of fresh snow works much like the soft foam panels used in recording studios to absorb sound. The effect does not last forever, however. As snow melts and freezes again, its surface becomes hard and smooth, and it begins to reflect sound like a wall. But for a short time after the snow falls, the softness of the snow is what makes a snowy world seem so ___ to our ears.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 갓 내린 눈 결정 사이의 공기 주머니가 소리 에너지를 흡수해 거리가 조용해진다는 내용이므로 silent가 알맞아요. bright는 눈의 특징이긴 하지만 to our ears(귀에)와 맞지 않고, harsh는 다시 얼어 소리를 반사할 때에 가까워요.

items.passage: In most parts of the world, an old building is valued because its materials are old. The stones of an ancient temple or the wooden beams of a medieval hall are carefully protected, since replacing them would seem to destroy the building's history. A famous shrine in Japan takes a very different approach. For more than a thousand years, its main buildings have been completely rebuilt every twenty years on a site next to the old one, using fresh wood but following exactly the same design. Then the old buildings are taken down. At first, this seems to throw history away. Yet the practice protects something that stone and wood cannot. Every twenty years, master carpenters pass their techniques on to young workers, who will one day teach the next generation. Twenty years is short enough that some workers can take part twice in their lives, first as learners and later as teachers. What survives at this shrine, then, is not the original material but ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the exact location where it was first built
the memory of those who once worshipped there
the beauty of the natural forest around it
the living knowledge of how to build it
the respect people feel for very old objects
items.exp: 20년마다 새로 지으면서 숙련된 목수가 젊은 일꾼에게 기술을 전하고, 그들이 다시 다음 세대를 가르친다고 했어요. 그래서 남는 것은 원래 재료가 아니라 짓는 방법에 대한 살아 있는 지식이에요. ①은 옛 건물 옆 부지에 새로 짓는다는 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Today we take house numbers for granted, but for most of history, homes had no numbers at all. People described locations by landmarks, such as "the house beside the old well" or "the shop opposite the church." ① As towns grew larger in eighteenth-century Europe, however, this system became difficult for governments to manage. ② Many of the grand houses of that period were decorated with carved stone and large windows facing the street. ③ Officials who collected taxes or counted men for military service needed a reliable way to find every household. ④ As a result, rulers in several countries ordered that each building be marked with a number. ⑤ Residents did not always welcome the change, since a number on the door made it easier for the state to keep an eye on them.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 집 번호가 생겨난 이유(도시 성장, 세금·병역 관리)를 설명하는 글인데, ②는 그 시대 대저택의 장식을 말해 흐름에서 벗어나요. ②를 빼면 ①의 관리 어려움이 ③의 관리들의 필요로 자연스럽게 이어져요.

items.passage:
In nineteenth-century cities, the most desirable rooms in an apartment building were on the lower floors. Climbing many flights of stairs every day was tiring, so the top floors were left to servants, poor students, and struggling artists.

(A) This began to change after the safety elevator appeared in the 1850s. Earlier lifts had been dangerous, since a broken rope could send them crashing to the ground, but the new design included a brake that stopped the car if the rope failed.

(B) The result was a complete reversal of the old order. Today, the most expensive apartment in a tall building is often the penthouse at the very top, the same place that was once considered the worst.

(C) As these safe elevators spread, reaching the top of a building no longer took any effort. Suddenly, the upper floors, with their fresh air, quiet, and wide views over the noisy streets, became the most attractive places to live.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 위층을 꺼리던 상황이 This began to change로 바뀌기 시작했다며 안전 엘리베이터를 소개하는 (A)가 먼저 와요. these safe elevators가 퍼지며 위층이 가장 인기 있는 곳이 되었다는 (C)가 이어지고, 그 결과(The result) 옛 질서가 완전히 뒤집혔다는 (B)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: Rumors often travel faster than the truth. A surprising or frightening story makes people want to share it right away, before they stop to check whether it is accurate. ( ① ) Corrections, on the other hand, are usually less exciting. ( ② ) A message saying "That story was false" does not create the same strong emotions, so fewer people pass it on. ( ③ ) As a result, many people who heard the rumor never hear the correction at all. ( ④ ) Even those who do hear it may continue to half-believe the original story, because the first version they heard has already settled in their memory. ( ⑤ ) For this reason, experts say the best time to fight a rumor is before it spreads, by sharing reliable information early and clearly.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

This lingering belief can shape people's opinions and choices long after the facts have been made clear.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 This lingering belief는 정정을 듣고도 원래 이야기를 반쯤 계속 믿는다는 ⑤ 앞 문장을 가리켜요. 그 뒤 For this reason으로 소문이 퍼지기 전에 대응해야 한다는 결론이 이어져요. ④에 넣으면 아직 남아 있는 믿음이 언급되기 전이라 어색해요.

items.passage: How can we remember new words better? In one study, students were shown a list of simple words, such as "apple" and "ladder." For some words, they were asked to write the word down several times. For others, they had forty seconds to draw a quick picture of it. The drawings did not need to be good; many were just a few rough lines. Later, the students were asked to recall as many words as possible. They remembered more than twice as many of the words they had drawn as those they had written. The researchers believe that drawing forces us to think about what a word means, what the object looks like, and how to show it with our hands. Each of these steps creates another path back to the memory. Interestingly, even students who said they were "terrible at art" showed the same benefit.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Drawing a word, even (A) ___, helps people remember it because it requires (B) ___ ways of processing the word.
items.exp: 그림은 대충 그린 몇 개의 선(a few rough lines)이어도 효과가 있었으므로 (A)는 roughly예요. 그림을 그리려면 뜻, 모양, 손으로 나타내는 방법을 모두 생각해야 해서 기억으로 가는 길이 여러 개 생기므로 (B)는 multiple이 알맞아요.

items.passage:
For decades, nutrition science studied food by breaking it into parts. Researchers identified vitamins, minerals, and other compounds, and then asked what each one did for the body. This approach produced important discoveries, such as the role of vitamin C in preventing scurvy. It also led to a popular belief: if a nutrient is good for us, we can simply take it in pill form and receive the same (a)[benefit].

Recent research, however, suggests that food is more than the sum of its nutrients. The same nutrient can behave quite differently depending on the food that (b)[contains] it. Scientists call this structure the "food matrix." For instance, the fat in whole nuts is partly trapped inside cell walls, so the body absorbs less of it than the nutrition label suggests. Similarly, eating a whole apple raises blood sugar more (c)[gently] than drinking the same amount of sugar in apple juice, because the fiber and structure of the fruit slow digestion.

Large studies have produced similar warnings about supplements. Some vitamins that seemed protective when people ate them in vegetables showed (d)[greater] effects when given separately as pills. One likely reason is that nutrients in food work as a team, with many compounds supporting one another in ways that a single isolated substance cannot copy.

None of this means supplements are useless; people with specific deficiencies may truly need them. But the lesson is clear: when it comes to eating well, the whole food, not the isolated nutrient, should be our (e)[starting] point.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Whole Foods Are More Than Their Nutrients
Vitamin C: The Discovery That Changed Medicine
How to Choose the Right Supplement for You
Nuts and Apples: The Healthiest Snacks
items.exp: 같은 영양소라도 어떤 음식 속에 있는지(식품 매트릭스)에 따라 다르게 작용하며, 영양소만 따로 떼어 낸 알약은 같은 효과를 내지 못한다는 글이에요. 그래서 '온전한 음식이 영양소의 합보다 더 큰 이유'가 알맞아요. ②, ④는 일부 예시에 불과해요.

One likely reason is that nutrients in food work as a team, with many compounds supporting one another in ways that a single isolated substance cannot copy.

None of this means supplements are useless; people with specific deficiencies may truly need them. But the lesson is clear: when it comes to eating well, the whole food, not the isolated nutrient, should be our (e)[starting] point.
items.q: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 보충제에 대한 '경고'가 나왔고, 따로 떼어 낸 물질은 음식 속 영양소의 협력을 흉내 내지 못한다고 했으므로 알약의 효과는 오히려 작았어요. (d) greater는 little이나 weaker로 바꿔야 해요.

items.passage:
(A)
Ethan had never wanted to go camping. When his grandfather suggested a weekend at Pine Lake, Ethan imagined mosquitoes, cold food, and no Wi-Fi. But his parents were away on a business trip, so (a)[he] had no choice. On Saturday morning, he climbed into his grandfather's old truck with his phone fully charged, planning to spend most of the trip watching videos inside the tent.

(B)
On Sunday afternoon, as they packed up the tent, Ethan noticed that his phone was still almost fully charged. (b)[He] had barely looked at it all weekend. On the drive home, his grandfather asked whether the trip had been as terrible as he had feared. Ethan thought about the falling tent, the smoky fire, and the sky full of stars. "Grandpa," (c)[he] said with a smile, "can we come back next month?"

(C)
When they arrived at the lake, Ethan checked his phone and groaned. There was no signal at all. His grandfather only laughed and handed him a heavy bag of tent poles. "Since your phone has the day off, you can help me," (d)[he] said. For the next hour, the two of them struggled with the poles and ropes. The tent fell down twice, and by the time it finally stood, both of them were laughing so hard that they had to sit on the grass.

(D)
That evening, his grandfather showed Ethan how to build a campfire. Following the instructions carefully, (e)[he] piled up dry twigs and placed a few larger branches on top. At first he blew too hard and put out the tiny flame, but on the third try the fire finally caught. They cooked sausages on long sticks, and Ethan was surprised at how good they tasted. Later, lying on a blanket by the water, his grandfather pointed out the stars one by one. Ethan had never seen so many; at home, the city lights always hid them.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 토요일에 출발한 (A) 다음에는 호수에 도착해 텐트를 치는 (C), 그날 저녁(That evening) 모닥불을 피우고 별을 본 (D)가 이어져요. 마지막으로 일요일 오후 짐을 싸며 집으로 돌아가는 (B)가 와요.

items.exp: (d)는 휴대폰이 쉬니 자기를 도우라고 말한 할아버지를 가리켜요. 나머지 (a), (b), (c), (e)는 모두 Ethan이에요.

items.q: 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 일요일 오후에 Ethan의 휴대폰은 거의 완전히 충전된 상태였다.
호수에 도착했을 때 휴대폰 신호가 잡히지 않았다.
Ethan은 첫 번째 시도에서 불을 붙이는 데 성공했다.
items.exp: (D)에서 처음에는 너무 세게 불어 불씨를 꺼뜨렸고 세 번째 시도에서 불이 붙었다고 했어요. 나머지는 모두 글의 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage:
Dear Ms. Harrington,

I am the leader of the Westbrook Youth Orchestra, a group of thirty high school students who practice in the music room of your community center. We are very thankful for the space you have given us over the past two years. I am writing because our practice time, Saturday from 9 to 11 a.m., has recently become difficult for many members. This semester, several students have been placed in weekend classes at their schools, and they can no longer arrive before 11. As a result, nearly half of the orchestra has been missing each rehearsal. I noticed on the center's schedule that the music room is free on Saturday afternoons from 2 to 4 p.m. Would it be possible for us to move our practice to that time? We would be happy to follow any rules that come with the change.

Best regards,
Kevin Moon
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 음악실 사용 규칙에 대한 설명을 요청하려고
음악실을 빌려준 것에 대해 감사 공연을 제안하려고
items.exp: 단원 절반이 토요일 오전 연습에 오지 못하니 비어 있는 토요일 오후 2~4시로 연습 시간을 옮길 수 있는지 묻고 있어요. 감사 인사는 도입일 뿐이고 공연 제안은 없어서 ⑤는 답이 아니에요.

items.passage: Minjun had been working on his grandfather's old radio all afternoon. It had been silent for twenty years, sitting on a shelf in the living room, and he wanted to surprise his grandfather by making it play again. He had cleaned every part, replaced two broken wires, and checked the instructions he had found online three times. Yet when he turned the knob, there was nothing but silence. Minjun pushed the radio away and dropped his head onto the desk. "Why won't you work?" he groaned. After a while, he picked up a flashlight and looked inside once more. There, hidden behind the speaker, was a tiny wire that had come loose. He carefully pressed it back into place and turned the knob again. A soft crackle filled the room, and then an old song began to play. Minjun jumped up, laughing, and ran to the door to call his grandfather.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Minjun의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 아무리 해도 라디오가 켜지지 않자 책상에 머리를 박고 투덜대던 Minjun이, 빠진 전선을 찾아 노래가 흘러나오자 웃으며 뛰어올라요. 그래서 '좌절한 → 아주 기쁜'이 알맞아요. ⑤는 감정의 방향이 반대예요.

items.passage: In a tennis match, a player may lose a point because of a silly mistake: an easy shot hit into the net or a double fault at an important moment. What happens next often matters more than the mistake itself. Many players replay the error in their heads as they walk back to the line, feeling angry and embarrassed. Their shoulders tighten, and their next serve is weaker. Before long, one bad point has turned into a bad game, and a bad game into a lost set. Top players have learned a different habit. Between points, they turn away from the net, fix their strings, and take a slow breath, as if closing a door on what just happened. Coaches say that a match is not one long test but a series of small, fresh chances. The player who wins is often the one who refuses to [carry the last point onto the court].
items.q: 밑줄 친 [carry the last point onto the court]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: play every point as quickly as possible
let a past mistake affect the next point
blame the umpire for a wrong call
practice the same shot over and over
change tactics after winning a point
items.exp: 실수한 점수를 머릿속에서 되풀이하면 다음 서브와 경기까지 무너지지만, 뛰어난 선수는 지난 일을 닫고 매 점수를 새 기회로 본다는 내용이에요. 따라서 밑줄은 '지난 실수가 다음 점수에 영향을 미치게 하다'라는 뜻이에요. ④의 같은 샷 반복 연습은 글과 관계없어요.

items.passage: Many schools have cut recess time to give students more hours for lessons and test preparation. This may seem like a smart choice, since more class time should mean more learning. Yet the opposite is often true. Children who sit still for hours find it harder and harder to concentrate, and their teachers spend more and more time calming them down. A break outdoors allows them to run, shout, and burn off energy, so they return to class ready to focus. Recess also teaches lessons that no textbook can. On the playground, children learn to take turns, invite a lonely classmate into a game, and solve small problems with friends on their own. These social skills matter as much as reading and math. Rather than seeing recess as time lost from learning, schools should see it as an important part of learning itself.
items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 수업 시간을 늘리면 학업 성취도가 높아진다.
교사는 학생들의 놀이를 가까이에서 지도해야 한다.
운동장 시설을 더 안전하게 고쳐야 한다.
시험 준비보다 독서 교육에 더 힘써야 한다.
쉬는 시간의 바깥 놀이는 집중력과 사회성을 길러 주는 중요한 배움이다.
items.exp: 쉬는 시간에 밖에서 놀면 다시 수업에 집중할 수 있고, 차례를 지키고 친구와 문제를 해결하는 사회적 기술도 배운다고 했어요. 그래서 ⑤가 요지로 알맞아요. ①은 글이 반박하는 생각이에요.

items.passage: Most of us read a book once and then put it back on the shelf, as if we had finished with it forever. Yet readers who return to a favorite novel years later often feel that they are reading a different book. The words on the page have not changed, of course. What has changed is the reader. A story about a father and his son may seem, at fifteen, to be mainly about the son's anger. At forty, with children of one's own, the same reader may notice the father's quiet worry on every page. Details that once seemed boring suddenly become important, and characters who once seemed foolish now seem wise. In this sense, a good book grows along with the person who reads it. Rereading is not a waste of time spent on something already known; it is a way of discovering how much we ourselves have changed.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the importance of choosing books suitable for one's age
ways to remember the plot of a long novel
how rereading a book reveals new meanings as readers change
reasons classic novels are difficult for teenagers
the role of parents in children's reading habits
items.exp: 책의 글자는 그대로지만 독자가 변하기 때문에 다시 읽으면 새로운 의미가 보이고, 다시 읽기는 자신이 얼마나 변했는지 발견하는 방법이라고 했어요. 그래서 ③이 주제예요. 아버지와 아들 이야기는 예시일 뿐이라 ⑤처럼 부모의 역할을 다룬 글이 아니에요.

items.passage: Since the first satellite was launched in 1957, humans have sent thousands of objects into orbit around Earth. Many of them are still up there, even though they stopped working long ago. Old satellites, used rocket parts, and even tiny flakes of paint now circle the planet at speeds of nearly 28,000 kilometers per hour. At that speed, a piece of metal the size of a coin can hit with the force of a speeding car. Space agencies already track tens of thousands of larger pieces, and working satellites sometimes have to change course to avoid them. The greater danger is that each crash creates more fragments, which can lead to even more crashes. If this chain reaction continues, some orbits could become too crowded to use safely, threatening the satellites we rely on for weather forecasts, navigation, and communication. Cleaning up space is difficult and costly, but ignoring the problem may cost far more.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The First Satellite: A Turning Point in History
Why Rockets Travel Faster Than Cars
Space Agencies Compete for Better Orbits
Space Junk: A Growing Threat Above Our Heads
items.exp: 궤도에 남은 낡은 위성과 파편이 빠르게 돌며 충돌을 일으키고, 연쇄 충돌로 궤도를 못 쓰게 될 수 있다는 위험을 다룬 글이에요. ①은 위협받는 대상 중 하나를 언급할 뿐이에요.

items.passage:
Maple Grove Family Board Game Night 2027

Put away your screens and enjoy an evening of games with your family!

• When: Friday, June 11, 2027, 6 p.m. - 9 p.m.
• Where: Maple Grove Community Center, Hall B
• Fees: $5 per family (snacks included)

What to Expect
• More than 50 board games will be available.
• Volunteers will teach the rules of each game.
• A short game tournament will start at 8 p.m.

Notes
• Children under 10 must be with an adult.
• You may bring your own games to share.
• Sign up online by June 7. Only 30 families can join.
items.q: Maple Grove Family Board Game Night 2027에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 집에서 가져온 게임은 사용할 수 없다.
items.exp: Notes에 함께 즐길 자신의 게임을 가져와도 된다(You may bring your own games to share)고 되어 있으므로 ④가 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 안내문 내용과 같아요.

items.passage: If a cat falls from a tree or a high shelf, it usually lands on its feet. This skill, called the righting reflex, ①[appears] when kittens are only a few weeks old. As soon as a cat starts to fall, tiny organs in its inner ear tell it which way is up. The cat first turns its head, and then it twists the front half of its body, ②[bringing] its front legs underneath it. Next, the back half of the body ③[follow], so that all four legs face the ground. Because the cat has a very flexible backbone and no fixed collarbone, it can make these turns in less than a second. Finally, it arches its back and spreads its legs, ④[which] helps soften the landing. However, this does not mean that cats never get hurt. A fall from a low height can be dangerous because the cat may not have enough time ⑤[to turn] completely.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: 주어 the back half of the body는 단수이므로 ③ follow는 follows로 고쳐야 해요. ①은 단수 주어 This skill의 동사, ②는 동시 동작을 나타내는 분사구문, ④는 앞 절 전체를 받는 관계대명사, ⑤는 time을 꾸미는 to부정사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Some cities have made their buses and trams completely free. At first, this seems like an expensive gift, since the city must pay for the service with tax money instead of fares. Supporters, however, argue that the policy brings many ①[benefits]. Without tickets, buses can load passengers faster, because no one has to stop at the door to pay. People with low incomes can ②[reach] jobs, schools, and hospitals more easily. Some drivers also leave their cars at home, which can ③[reduce] traffic and air pollution. Yet the results are not always as good as hoped. In several cities, most new riders were people who used to walk or ride bicycles, not drivers, so the policy did little to ④[increase] the number of cars on the road. Critics say that the money might be better spent on making buses more frequent and reliable. For many riders, a bus that comes on time may ⑤[matter] more than a free one.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 새 승객 대부분이 원래 걷거나 자전거를 타던 사람이어서 운전자가 줄지 않았다는 흐름이므로, 정책이 도로의 자동차 수를 '줄이는' 데 별 도움이 되지 않았다고 해야 해요. 따라서 ④ increase는 reduce로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 장점, 접근, 감소, 중요하다는 흐름에 맞아요.

items.passage: Blow a soap bubble through a wand of any shape, such as a square, a star, or a heart, and the bubble that floats away will always be round. Why does this happen? The answer lies in the thin film of soapy water that forms the bubble. The water in the film pulls inward on itself, trying to take up as little surface as possible. At the same time, the air trapped inside pushes outward equally in every direction. Of all possible shapes, a sphere is the one that holds a given amount of air with the smallest surface. So no matter how the bubble begins, the film quickly pulls itself into a ball. In this sense, a bubble's roundness is a result of ___: nature's tendency to use the least material to do the job.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 비눗방울 막은 가능한 한 적은 표면을 차지하려 하고, 구는 같은 양의 공기를 가장 작은 표면으로 담는 모양이라고 했어요. 빈칸 뒤의 '가장 적은 재료로 일을 해내는 경향'이 바로 ① efficiency(효율성)예요. ③ chance는 어떤 모양의 막대로 불어도 항상 둥글다는 내용과 반대예요.

items.passage: In most sciences, an experiment can be repeated. If one chemist mixes two liquids and gets a surprising result, another chemist can buy the same liquids and try again. Archaeology does not work this way. To study a buried site, archaeologists must dig it up, and digging removes each layer of soil, along with the exact position of every object within it, forever. Once a pot has been lifted out, no one can ever see again how it lay beside the bones and ashes around it. This is why archaeologists record every detail as they dig, with photographs, drawings, and measurements. It is also why many of them now choose to leave part of a site untouched, trusting that future researchers will have better tools for reading it. An excavation, in other words, is an experiment that ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: proves what earlier archaeologists already believed
requires expensive tools that few countries can afford
becomes more accurate each time it is repeated
depends mainly on the luck of finding treasure
can be carried out only once, since it destroys what it studies
items.exp: 다른 과학 실험과 달리 발굴은 흙층과 유물의 위치를 영원히 없애므로 다시 할 수 없어요. 그래서 모든 것을 기록하고 일부를 남겨 둔다는 글이므로 '연구 대상을 파괴하기 때문에 단 한 번만 할 수 있다'는 ⑤가 알맞아요. ③은 반복할수록 정확해진다는 뜻이라 글과 반대예요.

items.passage: Long before refrigerators existed, people around the world found a clever way to keep food from spoiling: fermentation. By allowing certain helpful bacteria and yeasts to grow, they could turn fresh food into something that lasted for months. ① Cabbage became sauerkraut or kimchi, milk became yogurt or cheese, and soybeans became soy sauce. ② These microbes produce acids or alcohol that make it difficult for harmful bacteria to survive. ③ Fermentation also changes the flavor of food, giving it the sour or rich taste that many people now love. ④ Some fermented foods even became more nutritious, as the microbes created new vitamins during the process. ⑤ Modern refrigerators use far less electricity than models built several decades ago, which helps families save money. Thanks to these benefits, fermented foods remain part of daily meals in many cultures today.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 냉장고 이전에 음식을 보존하던 발효의 원리와 장점을 설명하는 글인데, ⑤는 현대 냉장고의 전기 효율을 말해 흐름에서 벗어나요. ⑤를 빼면 영양 증가라는 장점이 'these benefits'로 자연스럽게 이어져요.

items.passage:
Living next to a volcano sounds dangerous, and it is. Yet millions of people around the world choose to farm on the slopes of active volcanoes.

(A) Over hundreds of years, however, this rock slowly breaks down. Rain, wind, and the roots of small plants turn it into fine soil that is rich in minerals such as potassium and phosphorus.

(B) The reason lies in what volcanoes leave behind. When a volcano erupts, it covers the land with ash and lava, which harden into dark rock where at first almost nothing can grow.

(C) Crops grown in such soil often produce excellent harvests. For many farming families, this richness is worth the risk of living in the shadow of a mountain that may one day erupt again.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 사람들이 화산 비탈에서 농사짓는 이유를 묻는 주어진 글 다음에 The reason으로 시작하는 (B)가 와요. (B)의 단단한 바위를 this rock으로 받는 (A)가 이어지고, (A)의 비옥한 흙을 such soil로 받는 (C)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: Many people enjoy cracking their knuckles, while others cannot stand the popping noise. Most of them assume that the sound comes from bones knocking against each other. ( ① ) Our finger joints are surrounded by a small sac filled with a thick fluid that keeps the bones moving smoothly. ( ② ) When you pull or bend a finger sharply, the space inside the joint suddenly grows, and the pressure of the fluid drops. ( ③ ) This causes a tiny gas bubble to form very quickly, producing the familiar pop. ( ④ ) Because it takes about twenty minutes for the gas to dissolve back into the fluid, you cannot crack the same knuckle again right away. ( ⑤ ) Parents often warn that the habit will cause painful joints later in life, but studies comparing people who crack their knuckles with those who do not have found no such link.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

What, then, makes this sound? Surprisingly, the answer lies not in the bones but in the fluid around them.
items.exp: 첫 문장에서 손가락 꺾는 소리를 소개한 뒤, 주어진 문장이 그 소리의 원인을 묻고 뼈가 아니라 주변 액체에 답이 있다고 말해요. 이어서 관절을 둘러싼 액체 주머니를 설명하는 문장이 오므로 ①이 알맞아요. ④ 자리는 이미 소리가 나는 원리를 다 설명한 뒤라 질문을 던지기에 늦어요.

items.passage: In a study at a restaurant, waiters were asked to take orders in one of two ways. Sometimes they repeated each order back to the customers exactly as it had been spoken, word for word. At other times, they simply said "Okay" or "Coming right up." The food, the service, and the prices were the same in both cases. Yet the customers whose words had been repeated left noticeably larger tips, about seventy percent more on average. Other experiments have found similar effects. People who are quietly imitated during a conversation, for example when the listener copies their posture or gestures, later describe that person as more likable. They are also more willing to help others, such as by picking up pens that someone has dropped. The researchers believe that being imitated makes us feel understood and connected, even when we do not consciously notice the imitation.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

When others (A) ___ our words or actions, we tend to feel closer to them and treat them more (B) ___.
items.exp: 주문을 그대로 따라 말한 웨이터가 더 많은 팁을 받았고, 몸짓을 따라 한 사람을 더 호감 있게 보고 더 기꺼이 도왔다고 했어요. 따라서 남이 우리를 따라 하면(mirror) 우리는 그들을 더 너그럽게(generously) 대한다는 ②가 알맞아요.

items.passage:
Ask people who invented the steam engine, and many will answer James Watt. The story of a lone genius with a sudden brilliant idea is easy to remember, but it is rarely accurate. Watt did not create the steam engine from nothing. Engines powered by steam had already been pumping water out of mines for more than fifty years. What Watt did was (a)[improve] an existing design, adding a separate part that saved a great deal of fuel.

Most important inventions grow in this way, through many small steps taken by many people. Each inventor (b)[builds] on the work of others, borrowing ideas, correcting earlier mistakes, and adding something new. In fact, when the knowledge needed for an invention is in place, several people often reach the same idea at about the same time. In 1876, for example, two different inventors in the United States filed papers for a telephone design on the very same day.

Why, then, does the myth of the lone genius (c)[survive]? Part of the reason is that a single name is (d)[harder] to remember than a long list of contributors. Patents and prizes also tend to reward one person, and stories with one hero are simply more exciting to tell.

Yet the myth has a cost. Young people may come to believe that inventing is only for rare geniuses and feel (e)[discouraged] from trying. Understanding that invention is a shared, step-by-step process makes it seem far more open to everyone.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: James Watt: The Man Who Saved Fuel
Why Patents Should Be Given to Teams
The Myth of the Lone Inventor
Steam Power and the Mines of Britain
items.exp: 와트도 기존 증기 기관을 개량했을 뿐이고, 발명은 여러 사람의 작은 단계로 이루어지는데도 한 명의 천재 이야기가 살아남는다는 글이에요. 그래서 '외로운 발명가라는 신화'인 ③이 알맞아요. ①과 ⑤는 예시로 든 증기 기관에만 초점을 둔 오답이에요.

items.exp: 외로운 천재 신화가 살아남는 이유를 설명하는 부분이므로, 이름 하나는 긴 공헌자 목록보다 기억하기 '쉽다'고 해야 해요. 그래서 (d) harder는 easier로 바꿔야 해요. (e) discouraged는 천재만 발명할 수 있다고 믿어 시도를 단념한다는 뜻으로 알맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
When Leo's family moved from a small town to a busy city, he hated almost everything about it. The streets were loud, the buildings were tall, and nobody seemed to say hello. At his new school, the other students already had their own groups of friends. He missed his old friends, the quiet roads, and the empty parking lot where he used to skateboard after school. For the first two weeks, (a)[he] ate lunch alone and counted the days until the weekend, wishing he could simply go back.

(B)
The next Saturday, Leo brought his own skateboard to the park. Marcus introduced him to three other boys, and they spent the whole afternoon practicing together. When Leo finally landed a trick he had been trying for months, everyone cheered. Walking home that evening, (b)[he] noticed that the noisy streets no longer bothered him. For the first time, the city felt a little like (c)[his] home.

(C)
One afternoon, his mother sent him to buy bread at a bakery a few blocks away. On the way back, Leo passed a small park where a group of teenagers were skateboarding. He stopped to watch. Their boards clattered against the concrete, and the sound reminded him of home. A tall boy with a red cap tried a jump, fell hard, and laughed as he got up. Noticing Leo watching, (d)[he] called out, "Do you skate?"

(D)
Leo hesitated. Back in his old town, he had skated almost every day, but he had not touched his board since the move. "A little," he answered. The boy, whose name was Marcus, held out his own board. "Show me," he said. Leo stepped on, rolled forward, and performed a simple turn. Marcus nodded with approval. "We're here every Saturday," he said. "You should come." Holding the bag of bread, (e)[he] walked home faster than he had walked anywhere in weeks.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 새 도시에서 외로운 (A) 다음, 빵을 사러 갔다가 공원에서 스케이트보드 타는 아이들을 만나는 (C)가 와요. Marcus의 질문에 대답하고 토요일에 오라는 말을 듣는 (D)가 이어지고, The next Saturday로 시작하는 (B)가 마지막이에요.
