Turn the beach into an outdoor art gallery! Teams of all ages are invited to create amazing sculptures using only sand and water.

• When: Saturday, August 14, 2027, 9:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.
• Where: Bayside Beach, near Lifeguard Tower 3
• Fees: $10 per team (2 to 4 members)

Rules
• Only sand, water, and seashells may be used.
• Buckets and shovels will be provided, but teams may also bring their own tools.
• Each team will have a 3 m × 3 m area.

Notes
• Register online by August 7. On-site registration is not available.
• Prizes will be given in two groups: Family and Youth (ages 13–18).
• If it rains, the contest will be moved to Sunday, August 15.
items.q: Bayside Sand Sculpture Contest 2027에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
items.exp: 비가 오면 대회를 8월 15일 일요일로 옮긴다(will be moved to Sunday, August 15)고 했으므로 취소된다는 ⑤가 안내문과 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 시간, 팀 인원, 도구 제공, 온라인 등록 기한과 모두 일치해요.

items.passage: Bees are well known for making honey, but their most important job may be one we rarely notice: pollination. As a bee moves from flower to flower ①[collecting] nectar, tiny grains of pollen stick to its hairy body. When it lands on the next flower, some of this pollen ②[is] left behind, allowing the plant to produce seeds and fruit. About one third of the food we eat, including apples, almonds, and blueberries, ③[depends] on this process. In recent years, however, bee populations in many regions have been shrinking. Scientists point to several causes, such as the loss of wild flowers, the use of certain chemicals on farms, and diseases ④[spread] by small insects. Farmers and gardeners can help bees by ⑤[plant] a variety of flowers and avoiding harmful sprays, so that bees have both food and a safe place to live.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: 전치사 by의 목적어 자리이고 뒤의 avoiding과 병렬을 이루므로 ⑤ plant는 동명사 planting이 되어야 해요. ①은 동시 동작의 분사구문, ②는 주어 some of this pollen(셀 수 없는 명사)에 맞춘 단수, ③은 About one third of the food에 맞춘 단수, ④는 diseases를 꾸미는 과거분사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Tennis is played on several kinds of courts, and the surface can ①[change] the game as much as the players do. On a grass court, the ball skids low and keeps much of its speed after it bounces, so points tend to be ②[short]. Players with a powerful serve often win there because their opponents have little time to ③[react]. A clay court works in the opposite way. Its loose surface grabs the ball, slowing it down and making it bounce higher. As a result, rallies last longer, and players need patience and strong legs more than a single big shot. Hard courts, made of concrete or asphalt with a smooth coating, fall somewhere in between, which is why many people consider them the most ④[balanced] surface. For this reason, few players win major titles on every kind of court; a style that is rewarded on grass may be ⑤[praised] on clay.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 잔디 코트에서 유리한 경기 방식이 클레이 코트에서는 오히려 불리할 수 있다는 흐름이므로, ⑤ praised를 punished(불리해지다)로 바꿔야 해요. ② short는 공이 빨라 포인트가 짧게 끝난다는 뜻으로 맞고, ④ balanced는 두 표면의 중간이라는 내용과 어울려요.

items.passage: Look out of the window on an airplane, and you will notice that it has rounded corners. Some of the first passenger jets in the early 1950s had nearly square windows, much like those in a house. Then, in 1954, two of these planes broke apart in the air. Investigators discovered that the trouble began near the corners of openings in the body of the plane. Each time a plane climbs, the air pressure inside the cabin pushes outward on its thin metal skin, and when it lands, the pressure is released. Over thousands of flights, this repeated stress gathered at the sharp corners, where tiny cracks formed and slowly grew. A curved edge, on the other hand, spreads the force evenly along its whole length, so no single point carries too much. Engineers learned an important lesson: in a structure under repeated pressure, sharp corners tend to ___ stress rather than share it.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 반복되는 압력이 날카로운 모서리에 모여 균열이 생겼고, 곡선은 힘을 고르게 퍼뜨린다고 했으므로 모서리는 응력을 나누지 않고 한곳에 모은다는 concentrate가 알맞아요. reduce나 absorb는 모서리가 문제를 일으켰다는 내용과 반대예요.

items.passage: Chess is a game of pure skill: no dice are rolled and no cards are hidden, so the stronger player almost always wins. That sounds fair, but it creates a problem for groups of friends with different abilities. A beginner who sits down with an expert knows the result before the first move, and after losing ten games in a row, few people want to play an eleventh. Games of pure chance have the opposite weakness. When only the dice decide, an experienced player's knowledge counts for nothing, and the game soon feels empty to anyone who wants his or her decisions to matter. This is why many of the most popular board games mix the two. A lucky roll can let a newcomer beat the club champion tonight, while over many evenings the more careful player still wins more often. In other words, a well-designed game ___.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: removes chance so that results reflect only the players' effort
lets experts teach beginners the rules before the game begins
gives weaker players hope without making skill meaningless
rewards the player who takes the greatest risks on each turn
keeps every match short enough to finish in a single evening
items.exp: 실력만의 게임은 초보자가 포기하게 만들고 운만의 게임은 숙련자의 결정을 무의미하게 만든다고 한 뒤, 둘을 섞으면 초보자도 이길 수 있지만 길게 보면 실력자가 더 자주 이긴다고 했어요. 따라서 약한 사람에게 희망을 주면서도 실력을 무의미하게 만들지 않는다는 ③이 알맞아요. ①은 운을 없앤다는 것으로 글의 결론과 반대예요.

items.passage: Many parents sign their children up for piano or violin lessons simply because they want them to enjoy music. However, learning a musical instrument can benefit children in ways that go far beyond music. ① Practicing a piece requires a child to focus on small details for long periods, which helps develop patience and concentration. ② Reading notes while moving the fingers also trains the brain to handle several kinds of information at once. ③ Some researchers have found that children who take music lessons tend to show better memory for words. ④ The piano was first developed in Italy around 1700 and was originally called the "pianoforte" because it could play both softly and loudly. ⑤ Playing in a group, such as a school band, also teaches children how to listen to others and work together toward a shared goal.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 악기를 배우는 것이 집중력, 정보 처리, 기억력, 협동심 등 음악 이외의 면에서도 아이들에게 도움이 된다는 흐름이에요. ④는 악기를 다루지만 피아노의 기원과 이름의 유래를 말하고 있어 흐름에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
Most ocean waves are made by wind, which moves only the surface of the water. A tsunami is completely different. It usually begins with an earthquake under the sea floor.

(A) In the deep ocean, these waves can travel as fast as a jet plane, yet they are surprisingly hard to notice. They may be less than a meter high, and a ship passing over one might not even feel it.

(B) The danger grows as the waves approach the coast. In shallow water, they slow down, and the water behind them piles up, sometimes forming a wall more than ten meters tall that crashes onto the land.

(C) When the sea floor suddenly rises or falls, it pushes the entire column of water above it, from the bottom all the way to the surface. This creates a series of waves that spread out in every direction.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 해저 지진에서 시작된다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 해저가 갑자기 움직여 물 전체를 밀면 파도가 생긴다는 (C)가 와요. 그 파도(these waves)가 깊은 바다에서는 빠르지만 잘 느껴지지 않는다는 (A), 해안에 가까워지며 위험해진다는 (B)가 차례로 이어져요.

items.passage: When we hear someone speak a foreign language, it often sounds as if the words are flowing together without any breaks, like one long, endless word. ( ① ) We cannot tell where one word ends and the next begins. ( ② ) Surprisingly, our own language is no different when we look at the actual sound waves. ( ③ ) Recordings show that in natural speech, there are almost no silent gaps between words; the sounds run into one another without stopping. ( ④ ) As a result, we "hear" clear breaks that do not actually exist in the sound itself. ( ⑤ ) This is why learners of a new language often say that native speakers talk too fast, even when they are speaking at a normal speed. Until their brains learn the new patterns, they simply have no way of knowing where the breaks belong.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

Our brains, trained by years of experience, automatically cut this continuous stream into familiar words.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 this continuous stream은 ④ 앞의 단어 사이 공백 없이 이어지는 말소리를 가리켜요. 또 ④ 뒤의 As a result, 실제로 없는 끊어짐을 듣게 된다는 내용은 뇌가 소리를 단어로 자른다는 원인이 먼저 나와야 하므로 ④가 알맞아요.

items.passage: Psychologists have found that people often feel happier after spending money on experiences, such as a concert, a camping trip, or a cooking class, than after buying material things like clothes or gadgets. One reason is that the pleasure of a new object fades quickly. A new phone feels exciting for a few weeks, but soon it becomes just another part of daily life. Experiences, on the other hand, become stories that we remember and share with others. Over time, memories of a trip may even improve, as small troubles like rain or a delayed train are forgotten and the best moments remain. Experiences also tend to be shared with friends or family, which strengthens our relationships and adds to the joy we feel.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Compared with material goods, experiences tend to bring more (A) ___ happiness, partly because they live on as memories that we (B) ___ with others.
items.exp: 물건의 즐거움은 빨리 사라지지만 경험은 기억으로 남고 시간이 지날수록 더 좋아지기도 하므로 (A)는 lasting이에요. 경험은 다른 사람과 나누는 이야기가 되므로 (B)는 exchange예요. ③은 (A)가 brief라 맞지 않아요.

items.passage:
In a negotiation, the first number mentioned often has a surprisingly strong influence on the final result. Suppose you are selling a used bicycle. If you open by asking for 200 dollars, the buyer will probably bargain you down, but the final price is likely to stay somewhat close to that first figure. If you open at 100 dollars, the deal will tend to end (a)[lower]. Psychologists call this effect "anchoring." Just as an anchor keeps a ship from drifting far, the first number keeps the discussion from moving too far away from it.

What makes anchoring so powerful is that it works even when people know the number is (b)[arbitrary]. In experiments, participants who were first shown a random number before guessing the price of an item gave guesses that leaned toward that number. Experienced professionals, such as real estate agents, are not completely (c)[free] from this effect either. Their estimates of a house's value were influenced by the asking price they were shown, even though most of them insisted it had made no difference.

Understanding anchoring can help you on both sides of the table. If you are the one making the first offer, a well-prepared, reasonable but ambitious number can work in your (d)[favor]. If the other side opens with an extreme figure, however, do not let it quietly shape your thinking. Instead of adjusting your offer slightly from their number, (e)[accept] it as a reference point altogether and return the discussion to your own research about what the item is really worth.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why the Lowest Price Always Wins a Deal
The First Number: A Quiet Force in Negotiation
How Professionals Avoid Mistakes in Pricing
Selling Used Goods Online Made Easy
Random Numbers and the Science of Luck
items.exp: 협상에서 처음 제시된 숫자가 기준점이 되어 최종 결과에 큰 영향을 준다는 앵커링 효과와 그 활용법을 다룬 글이므로 ②가 알맞아요. ③은 전문가도 이 효과에서 자유롭지 않다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.exp: 상대가 극단적인 숫자를 제시하면 그 숫자에서 조금씩 조정하지 말고 자신의 조사로 논의를 되돌리라고 했으므로, 상대의 숫자를 기준점으로 받아들이지 말아야 해요. (e) accept를 reject로 바꿔야 해요. (b) arbitrary는 숫자가 임의적임을 알아도 효과가 있다는 뜻이라 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Minji had been the best speaker in the school debate club for two years, and she liked to prepare alone. So when Mr. Cho announced the teams for the city tournament, she could hardly believe her ears. Her partner would be Sora, a quiet first-year student who had joined the club only a month earlier and had never spoken in a single debate. Minji forced a smile, but inside (a)[she] was sure that her new partner would only slow her down. The topic was whether cities should ban cars from their centers.

(B)
From that day on, Minji began to listen to her partner. The two girls divided the work: Sora searched for facts and examples, and Minji turned them into powerful speeches. Every evening they practiced in an empty classroom, with Sora playing the opponent and asking the hardest questions she could think of. Slowly, Minji realized that (b)[she] was enjoying the practice more than ever, and that her speeches had never been so strong.

(C)
In the final round, the other team asked a tricky question about how many shops had closed in a city that banned cars. For a second, Minji's mind went blank. Then Sora quietly slid a small card across the table. Minji glanced at it, answered with exact numbers, and the audience burst into applause. When the judges announced that they had won, a reporter asked Minji for the secret of (c)[her] success. She pulled Sora forward and said, "Here it is."

(D)
At their first practice, Minji did all the talking. She wrote every argument herself while Sora sat silently, taking notes. In a practice round against two older students, they lost badly because Minji could not answer a question about traffic numbers. Afterward, as Minji packed up angrily, (d)[she] noticed Sora holding out a thick notebook. Inside were pages of carefully organized data. "I was afraid to interrupt you," Sora said softly. (e)[She] had been researching the topic every night since the teams were announced.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: Sora와 짝이 되어 실망한 (A) 뒤에, 첫 연습(first practice)에서 Minji 혼자 말하다 연습 경기에서 지고 Sora의 공책을 보게 되는 (D)가 와요. 그날부터(From that day on) Sora의 말에 귀를 기울이며 함께 준비하는 (B), 결승에서 Sora의 카드 덕분에 이기는 (C) 순서예요.

두 사람은 매일 저녁 빈 교실에서 연습했다.
결승전에서 상대 팀이 까다로운 질문을 했다.
연습 경기에서 Minji는 교통량에 관한 질문에 답하지 못했다.
Sora는 조사한 자료를 공책에 정리해 두었다.
items.exp: (A)에서 Minji는 억지로 웃었지만 속으로는 Sora가 자기를 방해할 거라 확신했다고 했으므로 짝이 된 것을 반가워했다는 ①이 글과 맞지 않아요. 나머지는 (B), (C), (D)의 내용과 일치해요.
